Our results also show that multimodal information generally allows more comprehensive and effective auditing of classifiers, while unimodal variants beyond image-only inputs exhibit strong potential in scenarios where resources are constrained.

title: Rethinking 3D Small Object Segmentation: Comparative Insights Between nnU-Net and Transformers
authors: Jianfei Liu, Vivek Batheja, Perry J. Pickhardt, Peter C. Grayson, Ronald M. Summers
abstract: Transformers have shown strong potential in medical image segmentation, particularly as foundation models. However, comparative studies indicate that nnU-Net, a CNN-based framework, often outperforms transformer-based models. This study investigates why nnU-Net achieves superior performance, focusing on small object segmentation in CT scans and examining the role of transformers in developing foundation models for medical image segmentation. Six transformer-based and two CNN-based methods were trained in the MONAI framework using identical data augmentations and training settings. nnU-Net employed its self-configuration strategy to automatically determine optimal parameters. Segmentation of calcified plaques and mediastinal lymph nodes was evaluated. nnU-Net achieved higher accuracy for both tasks, with a statistically significant improvement over transformers in plaque segmentation$(p<.001$). The self-configuration mechanism of nnUNet played a key role in optimizing CNN training. Within the same framework, MedFormer outperformed SegResNet$(p=.04$), which shares the same ResU-Net architecture as nnU-Net, suggesting that transformers may benefit from enhanced self-configuration strategies. Overall, transformer architectures remain promising candidates for developing foundation models and achieving higher segmentation accuracy through self-configuration in supervised medical image segmentation.

title: YOLO-US: A Unified Multi-Task Foundation Framework for Generalist Ultrasound Image Analysis
authors: Wenpei Liu, Leshui Dong, Zhihan Zhang, Xinyang Liu, Yulin Sun, Runnan He, Xiuyun Liu, Dong Ming
abstract: The inherent heterogeneity of Ultrasound (US) imaging impedes the development of generalizable medical models, whereas the clinical translation of Generalist Medical AI demands unified foundation models rather than task or organ-specific approaches. This study proposes YOLOUS, the official baseline for the FMC_UIA 2026 challenge, which enhances the YOLOv11 architecture with a custom C3_MViTBv3 backbone and lightweight MBTransformer blocks, achieving a balance between local texture extraction, global long-range dependency modeling, and computational efficiency. Shared multi-scale representations are dynamically routed to four decoupled, task-specific heads, which are optimized for segmentation, classification, detection, and biometric regression. Comprehensive evaluation across a heterogeneous benchmark consisting of 27 subtasks demonstrates state-of-the-art robustness, with a normalized IoU of 0.7955 for precise detetction and a normalized MRE of 40.63 for biometric measurement. Furthermore, in-depth analysis of segmentation performance under severe domain distribution shifts yields critical insights into the “heterogeneity gap,” validating YOLO-US as a scalable, mobile-friendly baseline for future ultrasound foundation models. The code will be available at https://github.com/LwpZoe/YOLO-US.

title: Leveraging Fourier Domain for Unsupervised Removal of Structured Noise in Fluorescence Microscopy Imaging
authors: Haosen Liu 0001, Edmund Y. Lam
abstract: Due to the practical limitations such as phototoxicity, fluorescence microscopy images are generally with faint signals corrupted by severe and complex noise, necessitating the denoising step to improve image quality for more accurate biological analysis. Recently, unsupervised deep learning techniques have attracted widespread attentions owing to their powerful capability of removing noise without the reliance of collecting clean images. Although existing unsupervised denoising methods such as blind spot networks are effective in suppressing spatially independent noise, developing unsupervised strategies for structured noise is still underexplored. Based on the observation that noise correlated in the spatial domain can exhibit independence in the Fourier domain, this work develops a Fourier-based blind spot strategy to enable effective unsupervised structured noise removal for multi-frame fluorescence microscopy imaging. The evaluation on publicly available real-world microscopy datasets validates its effectiveness in removing structured noise.

title: CURVFUSE: Field-Curvature-Aware Multi-Focus Fusion for Bioluminescence Imaging
authors: Yu Liu 0112, Ruyu Ma, Nassir Navab, Jian Cui, Tingying Peng
abstract: Field curvature, a common phenomenon that causes distinct regions of a specimen to come into focus at different axial depths, limits the usable field of view in optical microscopy. Although recent image fusion approaches locally compare the image quality of two inputs and identify in-focus pixels, they often produce spatially inconsistent focus measures considering the sparse cellular structures. Moreover, the long exposure time of methods such as bioluminescence imaging, an emerging field, makes the specimen itself nonstationary, as cells may move, deform, or die, which further complicates the fusion. Here, we present CurvFuse, a field-curvature-aware fusion framework that explicitly estimates a spatially coherent fusion boundary guided by the image formation prior of depth-dependent focal surfaces. Morphology-guided operations and structural constraints are further integrated to ensure boundary robustness against local deformation and to maintain structural fidelity throughout the fusion process. To the best of our knowledge, CurvFuse is the first bioluminescence fusion method that enables the expansion of the usable field of view without inducing artifacts. All implementations are made publicly available at https://github.com/penglab/CurvFuse.

title: DiGMa: A Dual-Domain Collaborative Framework for Efficient Temporal MPI Reconstruction
authors: Zining Liu, Gen Shi, Ziwei Chen, Jie Tian 0001, Hui Zhang, Jingying Jiang
abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a novel imaging technique offering radiation-free and fast imaging with promise for temporal imaging studies (e.g., vascular and functional imaging). However, MPI temporal reconstruction is challenged by per-frame noise and the cost of joint spacetemporal modeling. In this study, we first propose a dualdomain collaborative framework for efficient temporal MPI reconstruction, named DiGMa, to address the two main challenges. DiGMa performs signal-domain denoising via GCN-based inter-frame modeling, and image-domain enhancement via Mamba that efficiently captures long-range dependencies. The proposed method was evaluated on both simulation and measured data, demonstrating superior performance over traditional approaches. Besides, qualitative results indicate fewer artifacts and superior image quality, while the computational load of the model is also reduced. DiGMa thus achieves a favorable balance between reconstruction quality and computational efficiency for temporal MPI.

title: Semantic-Aware 3D Polyp Segmentation in Dynamic Endoscopy Scenes
authors: Jinhua Liu 0002, Wen Tang 0004, Yongsheng Shi, Dongjin Huang
abstract: This paper proposes the first 3D polyp segmentation method based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) for dynamic endoscopy scenes. A two-staged training approach, SAPolyp-NeRF (Segment Anything Polyp in NeRFs), is introduced. The first stage is to reconstruct the dynamic implicit field of soft tissue. Then, a multi-view self-prompt mechanism is employed to automatically predict 2D polyp masks for the rendered views generated by the dynamic implicit field. The second stage is a 2D-to-3D segmentation module, in which a view-alternating weak supervision strategy is introduced to train SAPolypNeRF for the second time using 2D polyp masks supervision aggregated from multiple training views to produce a dynamic 3D mask implicit field for 3D polyp segmentation. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves higher-quality comprehensive reconstruction and accurate segmentation of the lesion region than the state-of-the-art 3D segmentation methods, resulting in the best overall performance.

title: Direction-Guided Watershed for Adherent Cell Instance Segmentation
authors: Ruochen Liu, Yi Tian, Yalin Zheng, Yuxuan Zhao, Jingxin Liu 0005
abstract: Accurate segmentation of adherent cells remains a critical challenge in computational pathology. While relation-based modeling excels at pixel-wise prediction, its reliance on watershed post-processing renders it susceptible to noise, potentially leading to over- or under-segmentation in complex adherent regions. To address this, we introduce directional guidance to augment the watershed algorithm via two complementary modules: a Directional Disparity Boundary Discernment (DDBD) module and an Oriented-Attentive Watershed Augmentation (OAWA) module. Together with high-gradient pixel screening, DDBD forms a dual-cue edge screening by assessing directional disparity, effectively discriminating true boundaries from noise. OAWA then accentuates these valid boundaries by weighting the neighborhoods along their dominant gradient directions, guiding the watershed to focus on salient ridges. Extensive experiments on the CytoDArk0 dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across multiple magnifications, improving the accuracy and robustness of adherent cell instance segmentation.

title: Two-Stage Cortical Surface Reconstruction from MRI with Arbitrary Slice Thickness
authors: Zhongliang Liu, Wenxuan Wu, Sijin Yu, Zhuoyan Dai, Xin Zhang 0013
abstract: Reconstructing the cortical surface from brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is crucial for cortical surface analysis. However, existing cortical surface reconstruction (CSR) methods are mostly tailored for high-resolution MRI with specific parameters, whereas clinical scans often suffer from thicker slices and inconsistent resolutions. To address this, we propose a two-stage deep learning approach for accurate and robust cortical surface reconstruction from MRI with arbitrary slice thickness. In the first stage, we employ an implicit neural representation (INR) super-resolution method with cycle-consistency loss to unify MRI with varying slice thicknesses to a consistent thickness while preserving underlying statistical properties. In the second stage, we progressively guide the model to learn resolution-agnostic features through Progressive Gaussian Resolution Annealing (PGRA) and a dual-branch attention self-distillation mechanism. The proposed method demonstrates robust and generalizable cortical surface reconstruction across varying slice thicknesses on the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) dataset.

title: DDRT: Decoding the Dynamic Interaction of Hierarchical Brain Hubs Using Reinforcement Learning in Task fMRI
authors: Xuan Liu, Xuhui Wang, Sigang Yu, Huawen Hu, Shu Zhang 0001
abstract: Identifying pivotal hubs within brain networks and elucidating their role in the dynamic expression of functional networks is fundamental to understanding brain functions. Conventional methods are constrained by time-invariant models that overlook the dynamic reconfiguration of brain functional networks, making it difficult to disentangle transient emotional states from enduring affective traits. To address these limitations, we propose a universal brain analysis framework called DDRT and implement it on the emotion task. This framework employs a reinforcement learning methodology that integrates dynamic influence with static network topology to identify key brain regions within task-specific temporal windows, and characterize the dynamics of their functional expression. Based on the frequency and persistence of these identified regions, we uncover a three-tiered hierarchical architecture of network hubs. This hierarchy reveals structure-function consistency and features a tightly integrated core (Core/Flexible Hubs) competes with the Periphery Hubs for global influence. Our work offers a new perspective on the mechanisms of the brain.

title: Expert Model Guided Visual Programming for Radiology Report Generation
authors: Zizhe Liu, Moshu Xu
abstract: Automated radiology report generation requires complex compositional reasoning to translate subtle visual findings into coherent diagnostic narratives. Current models often fail to capture fine-grained pathological details, leading to generic or factually inconsistent reports. To address these limitations, we propose an expert model guided visual programming framework. It decomposes radiological reasoning into specialized subtasks. Each subtask is executed by a domain-specific expert model. We use a two-stage progressive fine-tuning strategy to fine-tune the model. This architecture enables the vision-language model to leverage the precision of specialized medical vision tools while preserving strong language generation capabilities. We show that small, task-specific models can effectively guide the training of large medical language models. Through our experiments, we show an improved state-of-the-art performance on IU-XRay and MIMIC-CXR datasets.

title: Unsupervised Adaptation from FDG to PSMA PET/CT for 3D Lesion Detection Under Label Shift
authors: Xiaofeng Liu 0001, Menghua Xia, Yanis Chemli, Georges El Fakhri, Chi Liu 0001, Jinsong Ouyang
abstract: In this work, we propose an unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework for 3D volumetric lesion detection that adapts a detector trained on labeled FDG PET/CT to unlabeled PSMA PET/CT. Beyond covariate shift, cross tracer adaptation also exhibits label shift in both lesion size composition and the number of lesions per subject. We introduce self-training with two mechanisms that explicitly model and compensate for this label shift. First, we adaptively adjust the detection anchor shapes by re-estimating target domain box scales from selected pseudo labels and updating anchors with an exponential moving average. This increases positive anchor coverage for small PSMA lesions and stabilizes box regression. Second, instead of a fixed confidence threshold for pseudo-label selection, we allocate size bin-wise quotas according to the estimated target domain histogram over lesion volumes. The self-training alternates between supervised learning with prior-guided pseudo labeling on PSMA and supervised learning on labeled FDG. On AutoPET 2024, adapting from 501 labeled FDG studies to 36918F-PSMA studies, the proposed method improves both AP and FROC over the source-only baseline and conventional self-training without label-shift mitigation, indicating that modeling target lesion prevalence and size composition is an effective path to robust cross-tracer detection.

title: Deepsrs: Enhancing Stimulated Raman Scattering Imaging Through Multi-Stage Deep Learning for Super-Resolution and Denoising
authors: Jiaxin Liu, Songxiang Xu, Yihuan Xu, Ying Chi
abstract: DeepSRS is a multi-stage deep learning framework designed to enhance Stimulated Raman Scattering (SRS) microscopy images by addressing both denoising and super-resolution challenges. The pipeline combines an autoencoder-based spectral denoiser with fine-tuned generative models—namely GAN and diffusion architectures—to achieve rapid, high-fidelity reconstruction. DeepSRS attains up to fourfold lateral superresolution, markedly improving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), structural similarity, and perceptual quality metrics. This integrated approach expands the analytical capabilities of nonlinear optical imaging and opens new avenues for biochemical visualization, histological interpretation, and quantitative microscopy in both research and clinical settings.

title: Mamba-Based Conical UNet for Metal Artifact Reduction of CT Images in Visceral Artery Aneurysms
authors: Junfeng Liu, Ziyu Yang, Qian Wang, Zhongmin Wang, Wei Huang, Jun Shi
abstract: Metal implants for visceral artery aneurysm interventions cause severe artifacts in computed tomography (CT) images. Although existing deep learning based metal artifact reduction methods have achieved promising performance, they generally cannot well extract multi-scale information under conventional UNet structures. To this end, we propose a Mamba-based Conical UNet (MCUNet) to improve the UNet by a symmetric spiral structure. In MCUNet, each node is a dual-branch module that combines Mamba and convolution blocks. This design enables effective multi-scale learning within a unified framework and captures long-ranges dependencies and local details for high-quality CT image reconstruction. Meanwhile, a Shapley values-optimized Feature Fusion Module (SFFM) is further developed based on the cooperative game theory to fuse reconstruction features from MCUNet, which employs Shapley values to quantify the contribution of each reconstruction feature for improving the performance of MCUNet. Comparative experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Shap-MCUNet achieves best performance.

title: Integrating Neural Differential Forecasting with Safe Reinforcement Learning for Blood Glucose Regulation
authors: Yushen Liu, Yanfu Zhang, Xugui Zhou
abstract: Automated insulin delivery for Type 1 Diabetes must balance glucose control and safety under uncertain meals and physiological variability. While reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive personalization, existing approaches struggle to simultaneously guarantee safety, leaving a gap in achieving both personalized and risk-aware glucose control, such as overdosing before meals or stacking corrections. To bridge this gap, we propose TSODE, a safety-aware controller that integrates Thompson Sampling RL with a Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (NeuralODE) forecaster to address this challenge. Specifically, the NeuralODE predicts short-term glucose trajectories conditioned on proposed insulin doses, while a conformal calibration layer quantifies predictive uncertainty to reject or scale risky actions. In the FDA-approved UVa/Padova simulator (adult cohort), TSODE achieved 87.9 % time-in-range with less than 10 % time below$70 \text{mg} / \text{dL}$, outperforming relevant baselines. These results demonstrate that integrating adaptive RL with calibrated NeuralODE forecasting enables interpretable, safe, and robust glucose regulation.

title: GIG-NET: Cascaded Graph-in-Graph Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification based on Multi-Modal Fusion in Glioma
authors: Haoyang Liu, Yuwen Zeng, Zhang Zhang, Arata Nagai, Kengo Takahashi, Masayuki Kanamori, Hidenori Endo, Kuniyasu Niizuma, Noriyasu Homma
abstract: The molecular diagnosis of$O^{6}$-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) is a critical biomarker for evaluating the prognosis and therapeutic response in glioma patients. However, current machine learning and deep learning methods for predicting MGMT status from multi-modal data suffer from limited classification accuracy and insufficient interpretability of inter-modal relationships. To overcome these limitations, a novel Graph-in-Graph Network (GiG-Net) is proposed to jointly enhance predictive performance and cross-modal explainability. The proposed framework constructs a Position-wise Multi-modal Fusion Graph (PMFG) to model correlations among MRI sequences and radiomic features, followed by a Spatial Relation Graph (SRG) that integrates fused multi-modal representations to capture spatial dependencies. Experimental results on the public dataset (UCSF-PDGM) demonstrate that GiG-Net achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art approaches. Furthermore, the proposed model provides comprehensive visualization analyses that elucidate how inter-modal relationships contribute to classification, thereby improving both performance and interpretability in multi-modal glioma diagnosis.

title: Intelligent Diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease by Integrating CT Segmentation and Multi-Dimensional Representations
authors: Hao Long, Na Deng, Dongni Hou, Wenyu Xing
abstract: CT scans of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) show spatial heterogeneity, making precise characterization difficult with traditional methods. This study proposes a deep learning model with a “segmentation first, then diagnosis” cascade framework for intelligent COPD risk stratification. In the segmentation stage, an Attention-Spectral Dual-Module (ASDM) is introduced to integrate frequency and spatial domain features, combined with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to optimize skip connections and enhance key feature extraction. A region-adaptive composite loss function is designed to improve lung parenchyma segmentation accuracy. In the diagnosis stage, a cross-dimensional feature fusion architecture is used, with 2D CNNs extracting local texture features and 3D CNNs capturing short-range spatiotemporal context. A Transformer module models longrange dependencies across slices. Experimental results show excellent performance in lung parenchyma segmentation, with a Dice coefficient of 0.973. The model also achieves an accuracy of 95.8% in COPD diagnosis, demonstrating strong potential for clinical application.

title: From Intensity to Anatomy: Optimizing nnU-Net for MR-to-CT Translation on SynthRAD2025
authors: Arthur Longuefosse, Javier Sequeiro González, Fabien Baldacci, Jun Seita
abstract: Magnetic resonance (MR) to computed tomography (CT) translation enables a non-ionizing alternative for radiotherapy planning and longitudinal disease monitoring. The SynthRAD2025 dataset provides a large-scale benchmark to evaluate cross-modality synthesis methods across anatomical regions. Building upon the nnU-Net framework, this work revisits its design for image synthesis and proposes key optimizations to establish a strong new baseline. We integrate architectural refinements, a two-stage fine-tuning strategy, and an optimized Anatomical Feature-Prioritized (AFP) loss that leverages pre-trained segmentation features to enhance anatomical fidelity. Best practices for AFP supervision are detailed, including segmentation model configuration and layer selection. Evaluation on SynthRAD2025 combines intensity and segmentation-based metrics, showing that our optimized model ranks first on segmentation performance while maintaining competitive intensity fidelity. These findings demonstrate that anatomy-aware supervision within general-purpose architectures substantially improves clinical relevance without compromising visual quality. Our code is publicly available at github.com/Phyrise/nnUNet_translation.

title: Introducing Transformer-Based Cascaded Classifiers for Breast Cancer Histopathology Classification
authors: Emilia López-Abad, Jorge Pérez-Martín
abstract: Computer-aided diagnosis of breast histological images supports the identification of tumors, which is of high prognostic value for breast cancer patients. This task remains challenging due to stain variability, limited annotated data, and class imbalance. In this context, Transformer-based architectures have emerged as promising models for digital pathology. We propose a framework of cascaded deep learning classifiers that simplifies multi-label classification by constructing a pipeline of three binary classifiers. To maximize performance, robustness, and efficiency, we designed a comprehensive hyperparameter tuning framework evaluating different optimization strategies, learning-rate schedules, and cross-validation schemes. Temperature calibration and optimized decision thresholds were applied to improve probability reliability. The models achieved mean balanced accuracies of 0.953,0.975, and 0.935 for the three stages, respectively. The complete pipeline reached a mean accuracy of 0.932, demonstrating accurate and stable classification across hierarchical levels.

title: Selective Visual Program Reasoning in Whole-Slide Large Vision-Language Models
authors: Wei Lou, Guanbin Li, Xiang Wan, Haofeng Li
abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) show potential in pathology image diagnosis but struggle with fine-grained feature extraction from gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs). To address this, we propose a two-stage framework that uses external visual programs to enhance visual input for pathology question answering. First, an LLM-guided visual program selection module trains the VLM to choose relevant programs and generate interpretable rationales. Second, the selected programs are executed on WSIs to extract detailed visual features, which are then fused into the VLM for accurate slide-level QA. We also introduce SlideVLM, a vision-language model backbone with a visual token selection mechanism designed for efficient WSI processing in both stages. Experiments show significant accuracy improvements on the WSI-level visual question answering task. Project link: https://github.com/Lewislou/SVPR.

title: A Benchmark Analysis of Graph and Non-Graph Methods for Caenorhabditis Elegans Neuron Classification
authors: Jingqi Lu, Keqi Han, Yun Wang, Lu Mi, Carl Yang 0001
abstract: This study establishes a benchmark for Caenorhabditis elegans neuron classification, comparing four graph methods (GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, GraphTransformer) against four non-graph methods (Logistic Regression, MLP, LOLCAT, NeuPRINT). Using the functional connectome, we classified Sensory, Interneuron, and Motor neurons based on Spatial, Connection, and Neuronal Activity features. Results show that attention-based GNNs significantly outperform baselines on the Spatial and Connection features. The Neuronal Activity features yielded poor performance, likely due to the low temporal resolution of the underlying neuronal activity data. Our benchmark validates the use of GNNs and highlights that Spatial and Connection features are key predictors for Caenorhabditis elegans neuron classes. Code is available at: https://github.com/JingqiLuu/neuronclf-gnn-benchmark.

title: Optimizing Paths for Adaptive Fly-Scan Microscopy
authors: Yu Lu, Thomas F. Lynn, Ming Du, Zichao Di, Sven Leyffer
abstract: In x-ray microscopy, raster step-scans acquire images point by point, while fly-scans move the probe continuously to increase efficiency. Existing fly-scan methods, however, do not adapt to sample features, often wasting time in uniform regions. We propose an adaptive fly-scan framework that prioritizes regions of interest (ROIs) and uses image completion to reconstruct unscanned areas, reducing scan time and exposure while preserving detail. Our multi-iteration approach employs two functions each cycle: a score function to select anchor points and locate ROIs, and an objective function to optimize them. The optimized anchor points define a shortest-path fly-scan, after which image completion refines the reconstruction for the next iteration. We show that our method deliver accurate reconstructed images with fewer than 30 % of the measurements needed by raster scans.

title: End-to-End Mandibular Reconstruction with Integrated Repositioning and Completion Networks
authors: Feng Lu, Chenfan Xu, Jiacheng Sun, Chi Zhang, Min Zhu, Zhiming Cui 0001, Dinggang Shen
abstract: Patients with mandibular defects require mandibular reconstruction surgery to restore both physiological function and facial morphology. Accurate preoperative planning relies on a complete mandible in its correct anatomical position. However, existing methods primarily focus on morphological completion, without considering anatomical repositioning, which can result in significant issues if the defective mandible is left in a compensatory malposition. This paper presents a novel end-to-end framework that jointly performs mandible repositioning and morphological completion. In the repositioning stage, we predict rigid transformations to restore the displaced mandible to its anatomically correct location. The completion stage then restores the repositioned mandible to its complete morphology. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method surpasses state-of-the-art approaches, showing strong potential for clinical applications in computer-assisted craniofacial reconstruction.

title: Unified PET Image Enhancement for Diverse Degradation Levels with Mixture-Of-Experts and Dynamic Prompts
authors: Yi Luo, Jianan Cui, Huiyuan Zhang, Yang Yang, Heran Shalihaer, Yuanjing Feng, Xinhui Su, Huafeng Liu 0003, Xiang Li 0001
abstract: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) images often suffer from suboptimal quality due to physical constraints and clinical trade-offs, such as radiation dose and scanning time. Thus, PET image enhancement using deep learning is of great importance. However, most existing methods are designed to handle a single degradation level and lack the flexibility to adapt to varying degrees of image degradation. Recently, the all-in-one image restoration paradigm has emerged, aiming to handle multiple types of degradation within a single model. Inspired by this direction, this paper proposes a unified model for enhancing PET images under various degradation conditions, including varying doses and scanning times. Specifically, we introduce a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) mechanism into the encoder of the Restormer network. This allows the model to adaptively select specialized experts for different degradations. We also employ dynamic and adaptive prompts in the decoder to guide the recovery process. The proposed method is validated on a dataset comprising 430 subjects with multiple scanning times. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches. It works effectively on PET images acquired under various scanning conditions.

title: Scale-Aware Curriculum Learning for Data-Efficient Lung Nodule Detection with YOLOV11
authors: Yi Luo, Yike Guo, Hamed Hooshangnejad, Zongwei Zhou, Kai Ding 0003
abstract: Lung nodule detection in chest CT is crucial for early lung cancer diagnosis, yet existing deep learning approaches face challenges when deployed in clinical settings with limited annotated data. While curriculum learning has shown promise in improving model training, traditional static curriculum strategies fail in data-scarce scenarios. We propose Scale-Adaptive Curriculum Learning (SACL), a novel training strategy that dynamically adjusts curriculum design based on available data scale. SACL introduces three key mechanisms: (1) adaptive epoch scheduling, (2) hard sample injection, and (3) scale-aware optimization. We evaluate SACL on the LUNA25 dataset using YOLOv11 as the base detector. Experimental results demonstrate that while SACL achieves comparable performance to static curriculum learning on the full dataset in$\text{mAP}_{50}$, it shows significant advantages under data-limited conditions with$4.6 \%, 3.5 \%$, and 2.0% improvements over baseline at$10 \%, 20 \%$, and 50% of training data respectively. By enabling robust training across varying data scales without architectural modifications, SACL provides a practical solution for healthcare institutions to develop effective lung nodule detection systems despite limited annotation resources.

title: XBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Visual-Language Explanations in Chest Radiography
authors: Haozhe Luo, Shelley Zixin Shu, Ziyu Zhou, Sebastian Otálora, Mauricio Reyes 0001
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have recently shown remarkable zero-shot performance in medical image understanding, yet their grounding ability, the extent to which textual concepts align with visual evidence, remains underexplored. In the medical domain, however, reliable grounding is essential for interpretability and clinical trustworthiness. In this work, we present the first systematic benchmark for evaluating cross-modal interpretability in chest X-rays across seven CLIP-style VLM variants. We generate visual explanations using cross-attention and similarity-based grounding maps, and quantitatively assess their alignment with radiologist-annotated regions across 36 types of pathologies. Our analysis reveals that: (1) while all VLM variants demonstrate reasonable grounding maps for large and welldefined pathologies, their grounding performance substantially degrades for small or diffuse lesions; (2) models that are pretrained on chest X-ray-specific datasets exhibit improved alignment compared to those trained on general-domain data. (3) The overall classification performance and grounding performance of the model are strongly correlated. These findings underscore that current VLMs, despite their strong classification performance, still fall short in clinically reliable grounding, highlighting the need for targeted interpretability benchmarks before deployment in medical practice. XBench code is available at https://github.com/Roypic/Benchmarkingattention.

title: Generation of Infant Brain fMRI Functional Connectivity from Asynchronous EEG Recording with Identity Consistency
authors: Xiaoshu Luo, Yitian Tao, Zihao Zhu, Chen Xie, Kaidong Wang, Yanhao Wang, Gaofeng Wu, Han Zhang 0002
abstract: Resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) is essential for studying early brain development. However, obtaining functional MRI data from infants presents significant challenges. Electroencephalography (EEG) thus serves a low-cost, easy-to-implement alterative on this purpose. However, the spatial resolution and specificity of EEG is inferior to fMRI, making its extensive usage greatly limited. EEG-to-fMRI transformation using deep generative models faces data scarcity (limited synchronous EEG/fMRI pairs) and generalizability challenges (performance degenerated when apply to new participants). To address these challenges, we propose an identity-consistent data synthesis approach from EEG to fMRI-derived rs-FC with asynchronously instead of synchronously acquired data. The central idea is to extract time-invariant, trait-related, inter-modular mapping that mainly focuses on brain connectomic fingerprints. To achieve this, we employ graph learning to extract EEG connectomic features and leverage contrastive learning to make extracted features capture infant's individual traits that is invariant to acquisition time so that such features can further generate rs-FC of the same subject with an trainable, adaptive spatial interpolator. Our method demonstrates superior performance than other competing methods with the data from a novel, multicenter, large-scale Chinese Baby Connectome Project (CBCP).

title: DPANet: Dual-Path Prior-Guided Attention Network for Few-Shot Intravascular Ultrasound Segmentation
authors: Junqin Luo, Yuxing Wei, Lei Du, Ming Wu, Jiaqiang Li, Cheng Zhao 0003, Xinhua Yin, Tianfu Wang 0001, Baiying Lei
abstract: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is a key modality for early detection of coronary artery disease, enabling the assessment of vessel morphology and plaque burden by delineating the lumen and the external elastic membrane (EEM). However, low contrast, blurred boundaries between lumen and EEM, and scarce expert annotations make accurate IVUS segmentation difficult. We propose DPANet, a Dual-Path Prior-guided Attention Network for Few-Shot IVUS Segmentation. DPANet combines (1) a prior-guided difference reconstruction path that independently segments the lumen and lumen+EEM regions, then recovers the EEM via set difference to sharpen boundaries in low-contrast areas; and (2) an Iterative Prototype Refinement (IPR) module whose Cross-Attention Aggregation Module (CAAM) dynamically aligns prototypes with spatial features, improving generalisation under few-shot supervision. Experiments on a private IVUS cohort demonstrate that DPANet improves the average Dice score by approximately 3% over strong baselines, while maintaining high accuracy and robustness under severe artifact interference, and offering a practical solution for clinical vessel segmentation.

title: Dualclip: Joint Cortical-Subcortical Representation Learning for Neurodevelopmental Disorder Detection
authors: Jie Luo, Pengcheng Xue, Ming Yang, Han Zhang 0002, Xuyun Wen
abstract: Early diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders is essential for understanding atypical brain development. Although structural MRI has become a widely used tool for disease diagnosis, existing 3D CNN-based methods often overlook the topological organization of the cortex, limiting recognition accuracy. In contrast, surface-based approaches typically ignore subcortical structures, preventing a comprehensive characterization of neurodevelopmental abnormalities. To address these limitations, we propose DualCLIP, a contrastive multimodal fusion framework that jointly learns cortical and subcortical structural representations. DualCLIP consists of two complementary modules: SurfCLIP, which integrates a cortical encoder and a text encoder, and VolCLIP, which combines a volumetric encoder with a text encoder. Both modalities are projected into a metadata-aware text embedding space, enabling semantic alignment while mitigating confounding factors such as age, sex, and imaging site. Experiments conducted on two datasets demonstrate that DualCLIP achieves state-of-the-art performance across all tasks, confirming its effectiveness for neurodevelopmental disorder detection.

title: Multi-Class Transcompletion: Geometric Deep Learning for Four-Chamber Cardiac Reconstruction From Cine MRI
authors: Zhengda Ma, Abhirup Banerjee
abstract: Cine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the clinical gold standard for assessing cardiac dynamics but typically provides only sparse 2D slices, limiting 3D analysis of cardiac anatomy and motion. We present Multi-class TransCompletion network, a geometric deep learning model for reconstructing four-chamber cardiac point clouds from cine MRI. The network jointly models inter-chamber topology and anatomical coherence through label-supervised point cloud completion, learning spatially consistent shape priors from 10,000 3D meshes derived from a statistical shape model. Embedded in an end-to-end automated pipeline, the framework reconstructs anatomically coherent fourchamber 3D cardiac meshes directly from cine MRI. Evaluated on the UK Biobank dataset under cross-domain conditions, it achieves substantial improvements in geometric accuracy and anatomical plausibility over the state-of-the-art, and shows strong robustness to slice misalignment and motion artifacts. Code and models will be available at https://github.com/MultiMeDIA-Oxford/Multi-class-TransCompletion.

title: Unified Ultrasound Intelligence Toward an End-to-End Agentic System
authors: Chen Ma, Yunshu Li, Junhu Fu, Shuyu Liang, Yuanyuan Wang 0001, Yi Guo 0002
abstract: Clinical ultrasound analysis demands models that generalize across heterogeneous organs, views, and devices, while supporting interpretable workflow-level analysis. Existing methods often rely on task-wise adaptation, and joint learning may be unstable due to cross-task interference, making it hard to deliver workflow-level outputs in practice. To address these challenges, we present USTri, a tri-stage ultrasound intelligence pipeline for unified multi-organ, multi-task analysis. Stage I trains a universal generalist USGen on different domains to learn broad, transferable priors that are robust to device and protocol variability. To better handle domain shifts and reach task-aligned performance while preserving ultrasound shared knowledge, Stage II builds USpec by keeping USGen frozen and finetuning dataset-specific heads. Stage III introduces USAgent, which mimics clinician workflows by orchestrating USpec specialists for multi-step inference and deterministic structured reports. On the FMC_UIA validation set, our model achieves the best overall performance across 4 task types and 27 datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, qualitative results show that USAgent produces clinically structured reports with high accuracy and interpretability. Our study suggests a scalable path to ultrasound intelligence that generalizes across heterogeneous ultrasound tasks and supports consistent end-to-end clinical workflows.

title: Ranking Xai Methods for Head and Neck Cancer Outcome Prediction
authors: Baoqiang Ma, Djennifer K. Madzia-Madzou, Rosa C. J. Kraaijveld, Jin Ouyang
abstract: For head and neck cancer (HNC) patients, prognostic outcome prediction can support personalized treatment strategy selection. Improving prediction performance of HNC outcomes has been extensively explored by using advanced artificial intelligence (AI) techniques on PET/CT data. However, the interpretability of AI remains a critical obstacle for its clinical adoption. Unlike previous HNC studies that empirically selected explainable AI (XAI) techniques, we are the first to comprehensively evaluate and rank$\mathbf{1 3}$XAI methods across$\mathbf{2 4}$metrics, covering faithfulness, robustness, complexity and plausibility. Experimental results on the multi-center HECKTOR challenge dataset show large variations across evaluation aspects among different XAI methods, with Integrated Gradients (IG) and DeepLIFT (DL) consistently obtained high rankings for faithfulness, complexity and plausibility. This work highlights the importance of comprehensive XAI method evaluation and can be extended to other medical imaging tasks.

title: U-Harmony: Enhancing Joint Training for Segmentation Models with Universal Harmonization
authors: Weiwei Ma, Xiaobing Yu, Peijie Qiu, Jin Yang, Pan Xiao, Xiaoqi Zhao 0003, Xiaofeng Liu 0001, Tomo Miyazaki, Shinichiro Omachi, Yongsong Huang
abstract: In clinical practice, medical segmentation datasets are often limited and heterogeneous, with variations in modalities, protocols, and anatomical targets across institutions. Existing deep learning models struggle to jointly learn from such diverse data, often sacrificing either generalization or domain-specific knowledge. To overcome these challenges, we propose a joint training method called Universal Harmonization (U-Harmony), which can be integrated into deep learning-based architectures with a domain-gated head, enabling a single segmentation model to learn from heterogeneous datasets simultaneously. By integrating U-Harmony, our approach sequentially normalizes and then denormalizes feature distributions to mitigate domain-specific variations while preserving original dataset-specific knowledge. More appealingly, our framework also supports universal modality adaptation, allowing the seamless learning of new imaging modalities and anatomical classes. Extensive experiments on cross-institutional brain lesion datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, establishing a new benchmark for robust and adaptable 3D medical image segmentation models in real-world clinical settings.

title: Distilling Expert Surgical Knowledge: How to Train Local Surgical VLMs for Anatomy Explanation in Complete Mesocolic Excision
authors: Lennart Maack, Julia-Kristin Graß, Lisa-Marie Toscha, Nathaniel Melling, Alexander Schlaefer
abstract: Recently, Vision Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated high potential in computer-aided diagnosis and decision-support. However, current VLMs show deficits in domain specific surgical scene understanding, such as identifying and explaining anatomical landmarks during Complete Mesocolic Excision. Additionally, there is a need for locally deployable models to avoid patient data leakage to large VLMs, hosted outside the clinic. We propose a privacy-preserving framework to distill knowledge from large, general-purpose LLMs into an efficient, local VLM. We generate an expert-supervised dataset by prompting a teacher LLM without sensitive images, using only textual context and binary segmentation masks for spatial information. This dataset is used for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and subsequent Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) of the locally deployable VLM. Our evaluation confirms that finetuning VLMs with our generated datasets increases surgical domain knowledge compared to its base VLM by a large margin. Overall, this work validates a data-efficient and privacy-conforming way to train a surgical domain optimized, locally deployable VLM for surgical scene understanding.

title: Improving Gradient Flow Methods for Instance Segmentation of Crossing Objects
authors: J. Mabon, J. C. Olivo-Marin
abstract: In this paper we propose a novel flow tracking method for instance segmentation, that can handle crossing cells or objects. Current gradient-flow approaches (e.g. Cellpose, Omnipose) assign a single vector to each pixel; when flow tracks from different instances intersect, the vectors collapse onto a common trajectory, causing inseparable merges. Our new approach can infer multiple gradient-flow vectors at the same spatial location. By encoding the image into a latent embedding and decoding flow vectors conditioned on both the current pixel and its source position, the model can disambiguate intersecting flow lines and recover distinct instance masks even in scenes with many crossing instances. Evaluations on public microscopy benchmarks containing overlapping and elongated objects show that our multi-flow representation improves instance segmentation without sacrificing computational efficiency.

title: Deep Learning-Based Accelerated Adaptive Beamforming for Enhanced Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Imaging
authors: Midhila Madhusoodanan, Mahesh Raveendranatha Panicker, Abhilash Rakkunedeth Hareendranathan
abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) imaging typically uses delay and sum beamforming (DASB) for image reconstruction due to its computational simplicity. In DASB, the backscattered signals from the tissue are geometrically compensated for the time-of-flight (TOF) and apodized to reconstruct the final image. However, DASB images are susceptible to interference and are not optimized for any particular medical imaging use case. Various adaptive beamforming algorithms that leverage data covariance (like Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR)) have been developed to address the limitations of DASB. Despite their effectiveness, these algorithms are computationally intense and not suitable for high frame rate applications or real-time clinical use, especially for point-of-care US systems (POCUS). In this work, we propose a patchGAN-based beamforming accelerator for generating multiple plane wave (MPW) MVDR beamformed images directly from single plane wave (SPW) radio frequency (RF) data, learning both TOF correction and apodization. The model was trained and evaluated on in-vivo musculoskeletal (MSK) US datasets. The proposed model achieved a mean CR of 4.25 dB, CNR of 3.62 dB, and SNR of 6.00 dB, closely approaching MPW-MVDR (CR: 4.80 dB, CNR: 3.47 dB, SNR: 5.54 dB) while substantially improving over SPW-DASB (CR:3.25dB, CNR: 2.54 dB, SNR: 2.63 dB). Our patchGAN beamforming accelerator outperformed simpler encoder-decoder models like the U-Net by$5-10 \%$. This approach generated high-quality MVDR-like US images in 0.004 s vs. 148 s for conventional MVDR, which makes it well suited for real-time applications.

title: DBCoreset: A Density-Based Coreset Algorithm for Computationally Efficient Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
authors: Jayant Mahawar, Angshuman Paul
abstract: Coreset generation is a data reduction method that facilitates efficient deep learning training. A good coreset can achieve comparable performance using a much smaller number of training samples. However, traditional coreset methods exhibit density bias. This bias leads to poor representation of subregions that are sparsely populated by data points within a class. To solve this, we propose a novel Density-based Coreset Generation algorithm to facilitate computationally efficient chest x-ray diagnosis. We first partition the feature space into fine-grained, clinically-relevant miniclusters utilizing density. We then introduce a scoring-based selection mechanism. It helps in finding out the representative datapoints to eventually train a classifier model. Furthermore, we enforce a minimum inclusion criterion for every minicluster. This step aims to mitigate density bias so that coverage of all pathological patterns may be possible. Training the downstream classifier on the curated coreset demonstrates improved performance and balance. On the publicly available dataset, we used only about one-third of the training data and achieved a 40% reduction in computational resources. Even with this reduction, we have achieved as close as$83.01 \% \pm 0.36$with our method compared to$83.37 \% \pm 0.78$on the full dataset. We also outperform other coreset-based methods. Our method also reduces skewness in the classwise data distribution. The code is available at https://github.com/mahawar2/DbCoreset.git.

title: Unsupervised Detection of Post-Stroke Brain Abnormalities
authors: Youwan Mahé, Elise Bannier, Stéphanie Leplaideur, Elisa Fromont, Francesca Galassi
abstract: Post-stroke MRI not only delineates focal lesions but also reveals secondary structural changes, such as atrophy and ventricular enlargement. These abnormalities, increasingly recognised as imaging biomarkers of recovery and outcome, remain poorly captured by supervised segmentation methods. We evaluate REFLECT, a flow-based generative model, for unsupervised detection of both focal and non-lesional abnormalities in post-stroke patients. Using dual-expert centralslice annotations on ATLAS data, performance was assessed at the object level with Free-Response ROC analysis for anomaly maps. Two models were trained on lesion-free slices from stroke patients (ATLAS) and on healthy controls (IXI) to test the effect of training data. On ATLAS test subjects, the IXI-trained model achieved higher lesion segmentation ($\text{Dice}=0.37$vs 0.27) and improved sensitivity to non-lesional abnormalities ($\text{FROC}=0.62$vs 0.43). Training on fully healthy anatomy improves the modelling of normal variability, enabling broader and more reliable detection of structural abnormalities.

title: Automatic Correction of Generative AI Chest X-Ray Radiology Reports
authors: Razi Mahmood, Pingkun Yan, Tanveer F. Syeda-Mahmood
abstract: The factual correctness of generative AI-derived radiology reports needs to be improved before they can be used in clinical workflows. In this paper, we propose an automatic report correction method that uses both image and textual information in automated radiology reports to identity errors in identity and location in findings through fact-checking models. Prompts for a pre-trained large language model are then generated from the error analysis to produce corrected sentences by selectively modifying target findings described in the automated report sentences. We show that this method of report correction, on the average, improves the report quality between 17-30% across various SOTA report generators over multi-institutional chest X-ray datasets.

title: hSNMF: Hybrid Spatially Regularized NMF for Image-Derived Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: Md Ishtyaq Mahmud, Veena Kochat, Suresh Satpati, Jagan Mohan Reddy Dwarampudi, Humaira Anzum, Kunal Rai, Tania Banerjee
abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics platforms, such as Xenium, generate single-cell images that capture both molecular and spatial context, but their extremely high dimensionality poses major challenges for representation learning and clustering. In this study, we analyze data from the Xenium platform, which captures high-resolution images of tumor microarray (TMA) tissues and converts them into cell-by-gene matrices suitable for computational analysis. We benchmark and extend nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) for spatial transcriptomics by introducing two spatially regularized variants. First, we propose Spatial NMF (SNMF), a lightweight baseline that enforces local spatial smoothness by diffusing each cell's NMF factor vector over its spatial neighborhood. Second, we introduce Hybrid Spatial NMF (hSNMF), which performs spatially regularized NMF followed by Leiden clustering on a hybrid adjacency that integrates spatial proximity (via a contact—radius graph) and transcriptomic similarity through a tunable mixing parameter$\alpha$. Evaluated on a cholangiocarcinoma dataset, SNMF and hSNMF achieve markedly improved spatial compactness (CHAOS$<0.004$, Moran's$I>0.96$), greater cluster separability (Silhouette$>0.12$, DBI$<1.8$), and higher biological coherence (CMC and enrichment) compared to other spatial baselines. Availability and implementation: https://github.com/ishtyaqmahmud/hSNMF

title: Motion Compensation in Multiview Light Sheet Microscopy Temporal Series
authors: Grégoire Malandain, Haydar Jammoul, Kilian Biasuz, Patrick Lemaire
abstract: Temporal series of 3D images is nowadays a standard for the study of evolving phenomena (eg developmental biology). Multiple microscopy modalities can be used for this purpose: two-photon excitation microscopy, lightsheet microscopy, spinning disk confocal microscopy. Among these, the multiview lighsheet imaging allows to reconstruct a better resolved image by combination of several acquisitions. However, in this particular modality, the stage rotation may cause an extreme motion of the imaged sample, which, in turn, may impair either the fusion of the acquisition or the tracking of individual cells in the temporal series. We present here a methodology to retrieve these extreme motions, which enabled to reconstruct a stabilized temporal series of the fused images.

title: Reconstruction Algorithm Based on Multi-Harmonic Feature Fusion and Enhanced U-Net for Low-Concentration Magnetic Particle Imaging
authors: Yi Man, Ziye Ma, Yimeng Li

title: Visualization Guided Retinal Fluid Segmentation of Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans
authors: Saptarshi Mandal, Oindrila Haldar, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula, Raghu Prasad
abstract: Vision loss remains a critical global health issue, with conditions such as diabetic macular edema and age-related macular degeneration often detected only after substantial retinal damage. Early retinal fluid accumulation is a key biomarker, and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) provides noninvasive, high-resolution retinal imaging essential for diagnosis. Accurate segmentation of retinal structures is crucial, yet recent conventional deep learning approaches often do not provide satisfactory performance because fluid regions occupy a small portion of the image, leading to inefficient computation and reduced accuracy. We propose CLAVIS, a novel plug-and-play pipeline that leverages CLAssification outputs to generate VIsualizations and guide Segmentation, generating more precise maps of the fluid regions. We leverage visualization techniques to target image regions that influenced the classification outcome. Experimental results demonstrate that this guidance strategy improves Dice score by$\mathbf{+ 0. 1 4}$on the average and up to$\mathbf{+ 0. 1 8}$for some pathologies.

title: Biological Object Segmentation on Video Data Using Optical Flow-Guided Temporal Consistency
authors: Tristan Manneville, Raphael Reme, Jean-Christophe Olivo-Marin, Thibault Lagache
abstract: Biological videos are frequently affected by imaging artifacts, such as noise, motion blur, or low contrast, which can cause individual frames to lack sufficient signal for accurate segmentation. As a result, conventional single-frame approaches frequently miss faint or transient objects. We present FogNet, a lightweight multi-frame deep learning model that leverages temporal context in order to improve biological object segmentation on video data. Our approach combines simultaneous multi-frame predictions with optical-flowbased warping to enforce temporal consistency, while only requiring sparsely annotated video data for training. FogNet achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse datasets, demonstrating robustness to noise and large inter-frame displacements. These results highlight the potential of temporal modeling for reliable segmentation in dynamic biological systems.

title: Robust Circle of Willis ROI Extraction in MRA via Adaptive Landmark Detection
authors: N. Mansouri, Romain Bourcier, Florent Autrusseau

title: Data-Efficient Medical Segmentation Through Active Knowledge Distillation from a Sam Teacher
authors: Yuchen Mao, Hongwei Li 0004, Yuchen Pan, Giorgos Papanastasiou, Peng Qi, Yunjie Yang, Wei Pang 0001, Chengjia Wang
abstract: Large-scale foundation models such as SAM possess extensive visual knowledge, but their application to segmentation is hindered by their computational cost. Conversely, smaller, locally-hosted models like U-Net++ are efficient but require large labeled datasets. We propose an “active” domain knowledge distillation framework where a lightweight model, trained on limited labeled data, generates visual prompts (points and boxes) for a frozen general-purpose SAM “teacher”. In turn, SAM provides high-quality pseudo-labels from unlabeled data, which are then used to re-train the small model. Our method, using only 75% of labeled data, outperforms a fully-supervised U-Net++ trained on 100% of the data on two datasets. This framework enables the creation of efficient, high-performance models by leveraging knowledge continuously extracted from large models without expensive fine-tuning or inference costs.

title: Prompt-Free Lightweight Sam Adaptation for Histopathology Nuclei Segmentation with Strong Cross-Dataset Generalization
authors: Muhammad Hassan Maqsood, Yanming Zhu 0001, Alfred Lam, Getamesay Haile Dagnaw, Xuefei Yin, Alan Wee-Chung Liew
abstract: Histopathology nuclei segmentation is crucial for quantitative tissue analysis and cancer diagnosis. Although existing segmentation methods have achieved strong performance, they are often computationally heavy and show limited generalization across datasets, which constrains their practical deployment. Recent SAM-based approaches have shown great potential in general and medical imaging, but typically rely on prompt guidance or complex decoders, making them less suitable for histopathology images with dense nuclei and heterogeneous appearances. We propose a prompt-free and lightweight SAM adaptation that leverages multi-level encoder features and residual decoding for accurate and efficient nuclei segmentation. The framework fine-tunes only LoRA modules within the frozen SAM encoder, requiring just 4.1M trainable parameters. Experiments on three benchmark datasets TNBC, MoNuSeg, and PanNuke demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and strong cross-dataset generalization, highlighting the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed framework for histopathology applications.

title: Utility of Pancreas Surface Lobularity as a CT Biomarker for Opportunistic Screening of Type 2 Diabetes
authors: Tejas Sudharshan Mathai, Anisa V. Prasad, Xinya Wang, Praveen Thoppey Srinivasan Balamuralikrishna, Yan Zhuang 0014, Abhinav Suri, Jianfei Liu, Perry J. Pickhardt, Ronald M. Summers
abstract: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disease that affects millions of people worldwide. Early detection is crucial as it can alter pancreas function through morphological changes and increased deposition of ectopic fat, eventually leading to organ damage. While studies have shown an association between T2DM and pancreas volume and fat content, the role of increased pancreatic surface lobularity (PSL) in patients with T2DM has not been fully investigated. In this pilot work, we propose a fully automated approach to delineate the pancreas and other abdominal structures, derive CT imaging biomarkers, and opportunistically screen for T2DM. Four deep learning-based models were used to segment the pancreas in an internal dataset of 584 patients (297 males, 437 non-diabetic, age:$45 \pm 15$years). PSL was automatically detected and it was higher for diabetic patients ($\mathrm{p}=0.01$) at$4.26 \pm 8.32 ~\text{mm}$compared to$3.19 \pm 3.62$mm for non-diabetic patients. The PancAP model achieved the highest Dice score of$0.79 \pm 0.17$and lowest ASSD error of$1.94 \pm 2.63 ~\text{mm}(\mathrm{p}<0.05)$. For predicting T2DM, a multivariate model trained with CT biomarkers attained 0.90 AUC, 66.7 % sensitivity, and 91.9 % specificity. Our results suggest that PSL is useful for T2DM screening and could potentially help predict the early onset of T2DM.

title: Covariance Descriptors Meet General Vision Encoders: Riemannian Deep Learning for Medical Image Classification
authors: Josef Mayr, Anna Reithmeir, Maxime Di Folco, Julia A. Schnabel
abstract: Covariance descriptors capture second-order statistics of image features. They have shown strong performance in general computer vision tasks, but remain underexplored in medical imaging. We investigate their effectiveness for both conventional and learning-based medical image classification, with a particular focus on SPDNet, a classification network specifically designed for symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices. We propose constructing covariance descriptors from features extracted by pre-trained general vision encoders (GVEs) and compare them with handcrafted descriptors. Two GVEs - DINOv2 and MedSAM - are evaluated across eleven binary and multi-class datasets from the MedMNIST benchmark. Our results show that covariance descriptors derived from GVE features consistently outperform those derived from handcrafted features. Moreover, SPDNet yields superior performance to state-of-the-art methods when combined with DINOv2 features. Our findings highlight the potential of combining covariance descriptors with powerful pretrained vision encoders for medical image analysis. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/compai-lab/2026-isbi-mayr.

title: KOCOBrain: Kuramoto-Guided Graph Network for Uncovering Structure-Function Coupling in Adolescent Prenatal Drug Exposure
authors: Badhan Mazumder, Lei Wu 0013, Sir-Lord Wiafe, Vince D. Calhoun, Dong Hye Ye
abstract: Exposure to psychoactive substances during pregnancy, such as cannabis, can disrupt neurodevelopment and alter largescale brain networks, yet identifying their neural signatures remains challenging. We introduced KOCOBrain: KuramotO COupled Brain Graph Network; a unified graph neural network framework that integrates structural and functional connectomes via Kuramoto-based phase dynamics and cognition-aware attention. The Kuramoto layer models neural synchronization over anatomical connections, generating phase-informed embeddings that capture structure-function coupling, while cognitive scores modulate information routing in a subject-specific manner followed by a joint objective enhancing robustness under class imbalance scenario. Applied to the ABCD cohort, KOCOBrain improved prenatal drug exposure prediction over relevant baselines and revealed interpretable structure-function patterns that reflect disrupted brain network coordination associated with early exposure.

title: Intuitive Gradient Feedback: Continuous Ultrasound Scan Quality from Weak Expert Preferences for Probe Guidance
authors: Adam McArthur, Abhilash Rakkunedeth Hareendranathan, Jacob L. Jaremko

title: Harmonization Mitigates Diffusion MRI Scanner Effects in Infancy: Insights From the Healthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study
authors: Elyssa M. McMaster, Gaurav Rudravaram, Michael E. Kim, Trent M. Schwartz, Chloe Scholten, Jongyeon Yoon, Adam M. Saunders, Andre T. S. Hucke, Karthik Ramadass, Emily M. Harriott, Steven L. Meisler, Simon N. Vandekar, Allen T. Newton, Seth A. Smith, Saikat Sengupta, Kathryn L. Humphreys, Sarah Osmundson, Daniel Moyer, Laurie E. Cutting, Bennett A. Landman
abstract: The HEALthy Brain and Childhood Development (HBCD) Study is an ongoing longitudinal initiative to understand population-level brain maturation; however, large-scale studies must overcome site-related variance and preserve biologically relevant signal. In addition to diffusionweighted magnetic resonance imaging images, the HBCD dataset offers analysis-ready derivatives for scientists to conduct their analysis, including scalar diffusion tensor (DTI) metrics in a predetermined set of bundles. The purpose of this study is to characterize HBCD-specific site effects in diffusion MRI data, which have not been systematically reported. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of HBCD bundle metrics to scanner model-related variance and address these variations with ComBat-GAM harmonization within the current HBCD data release 1.1 across six scanner models. Following ComBat-GAM, we observe zero statistically significant differences between the distributions from any scanner model following FDR correction and reduce Cohen's$f$effect sizes across all metrics. Our work underscores the importance of rigorous harmonization efforts in large-scale studies, and we encourage future investigations of HBCD data to control for these effects.

title: Hybrid Resnet-Unetr for Semi-Supervised Fetal Cardiac Segmentation and CHD Classification
authors: Rodrigo Medellin-Robles, Flavio Alfonso Juárez-Castro, Mohammad A. Bukhari
abstract: We present a multi-task framework for simultaneous fetal cardiac structure segmentation (14 classes, 4 views) and congenital heart disease (CHD) classification (7 pathologies) from prenatal ultrasound, developed for the FETUS 2026 Challenge at ISBI. Our approach introduces a hybrid architecture combining a fully trainable ResNet-50 encoder with a UNETR-style decoder enhanced by deep supervision at four levels and a boundary detection head that fuses contour features into the decoding path. Classification is performed through a multi-scale attention pooling and a morphological feature head. We demonstrated that a two-phase trainable general-purpose framework can outperform a domain specific foundation model under label scarcity obtaining segmentation metrics of Dice = 73.32 and NSD = 48.76, while for classification Macro F1 = 32.64, with a score of 52.16/80., achieving first place in the challenge.

title: Channel-Agnostic vs. Channel-Adaptive: Foundation Model Strategies for Spatial Proteomics
authors: Hatef Mehrabian, Samantha Panakkal, Michael F. Sharpnack, Lauri Diehl
abstract: Spatial proteomics via multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) requires vision foundation models capable of handling variable channel composition and leveraging tissue structure information. Using DINOv2 framework, we trained and benchmarked channel-agnostic (standard ViT-s/14) and channel-adaptive (KRONOS-style ViT-s/14 with marker embeddings) architectures, on a large mIF dataset of 14,946 slides (48,993 single-marker images), 45 markers, and diverse tissue and disease types. Including the autofluorescence (AF) channel enabled channel-agnostic models to achieve consistently high linear probing F1-scores (BCL-2:$0.76, \text{HBsAg}: 0.69, \text{HBcAg}: 0.71$), compared to channel-adaptive (BCL-2:$0.61, \text{HBsAg}: 0.52, \text{HBcAg}$: 0.69) and reference models trained on H&E (UNI) or natural images (DINOv2). Channel-adaptive model performance fluctuated between tests (HBsAg (SD): 0.21), while channel-agnostic models remained robust (HBsAg (SD):$0.01)$. AF-containing models also produced more accurate tissue compartmentalization maps. Expanding training data further improved channel-agnostic model performance. These results establish the importance of AF and channel-agnostic ViT architectures for generalizable mIF representation learning.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Image Classification in Biomedical Imaging Using Spectral-Normalized Neural Gaussian Processes
authors: Uma Meleti, Jeffrey J. Nirschl
abstract: Accurate histopathologic interpretation is key for clinical decision-making; however, current deep learning models for digital pathology are often overconfident and poorly calibrated in out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, which limit trust and clinical adoption. Safety-critical medical imaging workflows benefit from intrinsic uncertainty-aware properties that can accurately reject OOD input. We implement the Spectral-normalized Neural Gaussian Process (SNGP), a set of lightweight modifications that apply spectral normalization and replace the final dense layer with a Gaussian process layer to improve single-model uncertainty estimation and OOD detection. We evaluate SNGP vs. deterministic and Monte Carlo dropout on six datasets across three biomedical classification tasks: white blood cells, amyloid plaques, and colorectal histopathology. SNGP has comparable in-distribution performance while significantly improving uncertainty estimation and OOD detection. Thus, SNGP or related models offer a useful framework for uncertainty-aware classification in digital pathology, supporting safe deployment and building trust with pathologists.

title: Right Collateral Sulcus Morphology Correlates With Receptive Communication in Preterm Born Adolescents and Neonates
authors: Racim Menasria, Julien Laval, Denis Rivière, Jessica Dubois, Jean-François Mangin, Joël Chavas
abstract: Preterm birth is associated with an increased risk of longterm neurodevelopmental impairments, including cognitive and motor difficulties [1], [2], yet robust morphological markers remain elusive [3]. Understanding how prematurity affects cortical folding and cognitive development is crucial for improving early detection and guiding targeted interventions. Here, we analyzed sulcal shape across 56 cortical regions using self-supervised sulcal embeddings derived from Champollion [4] to identify anatomical correlates of cognition in preterm-born individuals. Among these regions, the right collateral sulcus (FColl) showed the strongest and most reproducible association with receptive vocabulary, a measure of crystallized intelligence. Using preterm-born participants from two independent cohorts - adolescents from the ABCD study and neonates from the dHCP study we found that right FColl embeddings significantly predicted receptive communication scores and revealed a consistent mean-shape motif across development. These findings suggest that variability in right FColl shape may constitute an anatomical proxy, stable through development, for the underlying processes that subtend crystallized intelligence in individuals born preterm.

title: Boundary-Aware Instance Segmentation in Microscopy Imaging
authors: Thomas Mendelson, Joshua Francois, Galit Lahav, Tammy Riklin Raviv
abstract: Accurate delineation of individual cells in microscopy videos is essential for studying cellular dynamics, yet separating touching or overlapping instances remains a persistent challenge. Although foundation-model for segmentation such as SAM have broadened the accessibility of image segmentation, they still struggle to separate nearby cell instances in dense microscopy scenes without extensive prompting. We propose a prompt-free, boundary-aware instance segmentation framework that predicts signed distance functions (SDFs) instead of binary masks, enabling smooth and geometry-consistent modeling of cell contours. A learned sigmoid mapping converts SDFs into probability maps, yielding sharp boundary localization and robust separation of adjacent instances. Training is guided by a unified Modified Hausdorff Distance (MHD) loss that integrates region- and boundary-based terms. Evaluations on both public and private high-throughput microscopy datasets demonstrate improved boundary accuracy and instance-level performance compared to recent SAM-based and foundation-model approaches. Source code is available at.

title: Detecting Rare Cortical Connectivity Around the Human Central Sulcus: A Deep Learning Analysis of 37,000+ Tractographies
authors: Cristobal Mendoza, Nabil Vindas, Joël Chavas, Julien Laval, Antoine Dufournet, Pamela Guevara, Vincent Frouin, Denis Rivière, Jean-François Mangin
abstract: White matter (WM) and cortical folding are closely linked, exhibiting normal variability across individuals that reflects the diverse patterns of brain organization. However, identifying rare patterns remains a challenging task because they are largely hidden by the high inter-subject variability of cortical anatomy. In this work, we present the first deep learning framework for detecting uncommon arrangements of WM fiber tracts in a large population ($n=37,140$). To this end, we employed a$\beta$-Variational AutoEncoder ($\beta$-VAE) to learn meaningful latent representations of local WM connectivity. Leveraging the latent space for a classification task on an annotated subset of subjects with an interrupted Central Sulcus (CS) achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve above 0.9 across several$\beta$-VAE models. Furthermore, by analyzing the predicted probability of an interrupted CS, we identified a population-level transition from a continuous, stable CS to a more disorganized pattern characterized by branching folds and WM occupying the sulcal space. Code is available at github.com/neurospin-projects/bvae_fibers.

title: Anisotropy-Aware Strategy for Robust Deep Learning-Based Particle Picking in 3D Cellular Cryo-Electron Tomogram
authors: Mounir Messaoudi, Charles Kervrann
abstract: Particle picking in cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is challenging due to low signal-to-noise ratios, the Z-axis deformation and the “missing wedge” reconstruction. To address these challenges, we propose to enhance the dominant two-stage deep learning pipeline by prioritizing a coherent anisotropy-aware detection strategy. We also introduce anisotropy-aware Test-Time Augmentation (TTA), a technique not previously applied in this context. We demonstrate that the coherent application of anisotropy-aware augmentations during both training and inference improve the detection performance. Additionally, we evaluate the impact of deeper encoders, observing comparable performance to lighter models. Our work provides a clear framework demonstrating how these complementary strategies can be combined to significantly improve particle detection.

title: Distribution-Based Brain Connectivity Graph Representations for Classification
authors: Razan Mhanna, Sophie Achard, Alexander Petersen, Jonas Richiardi
abstract: Graph-based modeling of the human brain connectome from resting-state fMRI data has become a widely adopted approach in neuroimaging. Region-to-region connectivity is typically estimated using Pearson correlation between timeseries region averages, then used as edge weight in the corresponding brain graph. Instead of scalar edge weights, here, we use a vector of quantiles of distribution-valued edges from a voxel clustering-based statistical estimator. Using three resting-state datasets for classification tasks (patient diagnosis and fluid intelligence quantiles, total$N=293$), we compare the performance of graph representations with distributionvalued edges to that of scalar-valued edges, with six different classifiers - tree ensembles, graph neural networks, and a CNN-XGBoost approach. On metrics of accuracy, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, and AUC, our distribution-valued representation consistently and significantly outperforms classical scalar edge representations.

title: LognormalNet: Parametric Survival Model with Uncertainty Quantification via Evidential Likelihood-Based Inference
authors: Chunlin Mi, Thierry Denoeux, Pierre Vera, Su Ruan
abstract: Due to censored observations and multi-modal data heterogeneity, reliable survival prediction is a significant challenge for patients after cancer treatment. In this study, we propose LognormalNet, a parametric neural network that performs survival estimation and uncertainty quantification using evidential likelihood-based inference. The model captures the nonlinear relationship between patient covariates and survival time under a lognormal distribution. To characterize prediction uncertainty, we employ a random fuzzy set, derived by linearizing the network output and using a Gaussian approximation of the likelihood function. This framework can capture both aleatory uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty. Evaluated on the HECTOR2025 dataset, LognormalNet outperforms other survival models while effectively quantifying prediction uncertainty.

title: Jacobian Determinant Quantifies White Matter Plasticity Associated with SSRI Response in Depression
authors: Zhaoxian Ming, Yifei He, Yu Xie, Huangjing Ni, Zhijian Yao, Qing Lu 0005, Ye Wu, Jiaolong Qin
abstract: The neuroplastic effects of antidepressant treatment, particularly in white matter (WM) microstructural remodeling, necessitate precise quantification methods. We proposed an analytical pipeline consisting of three steps: (1) two-level partitioning to homogenize whole-brain WM fiber shapes, (2) large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping to gather deformation information, and (3) applying the Jacobian determinant to measure WM-specific shape changes. This method, tested on 51 SSRI-treated depressed patients, effectively detected treatment-induced neuroplasticity. When comparing the Jacobian-derived deformation metric to the traditional momentum vector metric and fractional anisotropy in terms of correlation with clinical improvement, the Jacobian determinant showed the greatest advantage. It identified more statistically significant correlations, particularly in reward, emotion regulation, and somatomotor pathways, as well as in certain connections within the default mode network. These results highlight the Jacobian determinant approach as a powerful tool for exploring antidepressant mechanisms and as a potential objective measure of therapeutic efficacy.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation with Target-Only Margin Disparity Discrepancy
authors: Gauthier Miralles, Loïc Le Folgoc, Vincent Jugnon, Pietro Gori
abstract: In interventional radiology, Cone-Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) is a helpful imaging modality that provides guidance to practicians during minimally invasive procedures. CBCT differs from traditional Computed Tomography (CT) due to its limited reconstructed field of view, specific artefacts, and the intra-arterial administration of contrast medium. While CT benefits from abundant publicly available annotated datasets, interventional CBCT data remain scarce and largely unannotated, with existing datasets focused primarily on radiotherapy applications. To address this limitation, we leverage a proprietary collection of unannotated interventional CBCT scans in conjunction with annotated CT data, employing domain adaptation techniques to bridge the modality gap and enhance liver segmentation performance on CBCT. We propose a novel unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework based on the formalism of Margin Disparity Discrepancy (MDD), which improves target domain performance through a reformulation of the original MDD optimization framework. Experimental results on CT and CBCT datasets for liver segmentation demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in UDA, as well as in the few-shot setting.

title: Cross-Modal Image Learning for HER2 Status Detection From H&E Histopathology Images
authors: Shubham Mishra, Debapriya Roy, Sandeep Mathur, Bikash Santra
abstract: Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) status plays a key role in predicting breast cancer outcomes and guiding targeted treatments. The current clinical standard, Immunohistochemistry (IHC), provides reliable results but depends on specialized reagents, extra processing time, and advanced laboratory facilities, making it less accessible in many settings.
