Unlike conventional attention-based MIL, which ignores spatial organization, or graph-based MIL, which relies on static handcrafted graphs, HMKGN enforces a hierarchical structure with spatial locality constraints, wherein local cellular-level dynamic graphs aggregate spatially proximate patches within each region of interest (ROI) and a global slide-level dynamic graph integrates ROI-level features into WSI-level representations. Moreover, multi-scale integration at the ROI level combines coarse contextual features from broader views with fine-grained structural representations from local patch-graph aggregation. We evaluate HMKGN on four TCGA cohorts (KIRC, LGG, PAAD, and STAD;$\mathrm{N}=513$, 487, 138, and 370) for survival prediction. It consistently outperforms existing MIL-based models, yielding improved concordance indices (10.85% better) and statistically significant stratification of patient survival risk (log-rank$p<0.05$).

title: RTFGM-Net: A Deep Learning Model for Auto-Detection of Hypsarrhythmia EEG in West Syndrome
authors: Chenghao Xue, Yifei Bai, Yuanning Li, Dake He, Lin Xu
abstract: West syndrome (WS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delays and motor spasms, often diagnosed through visual detection of hypsarrhythmia in long-term electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. However, manual analysis is time-consuming and prone to errors, underscoring the need for automated diagnostic approaches. In this paper, we propose ResNet-based Time-Frequency Gating Mamba Network RTFGM-Net, an efficient deep learning framework for automated hypsarrhythmia detection in EEG signals. The model integrates a Bidirectional Mamba (BiMamba) and an Efficient Frequency-Time Gating (EFTG) module. The EFTG module combines point-wise and depthwise convolutions with a learnable frequency-domain filter for effective feature extraction, while the BiMamba module captures long-range temporal dependencies through bidirectional processing. Experimental results demonstrate that RTFGM-Net outperforms existing methods, achieving an accuracy of 91.01% and F1 score of 90.33%, highlighting its potential to facilitate reliable WS diagnosis in clinical applications.

title: OpenEEG: Uncertainty-Aware Open Set Learning for EEG-Based Brain Disorders Diagnosis
authors: Li Xue, Weikang Gu, Jiaming Yu, Xuemei Qiu, Tao Wu, Lifang Wei
abstract: Deep learning models for EEG-based brain disorder diagnosis have shown promise, but their clinical utility is hampered by the restrictive closed-set assumption and an inability to quantify predictive uncertainty. This limitation leads to overconfident misclassifications of both unseen disorders and challenging known cases, posing significant safety risks. To address these issues, we propose OpenEEG, an uncertainty-aware open-set learning framework designed to simultaneously reject unknown disease categories and quantify the epistemic uncertainty of its predictions. OpenEEG integrates a Transformer backbone with a UA-Classifier based on evidential deep learning, which learns a Dirichlet distribution over class predictions to derive uncertainty scores. We validate our framework on multiple public EEG datasets under subjectindependent splits. The results demonstrate that OpenEEG substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both closed-set classification and open-set detection. By enabling principled rejection of unknown and uncertain diagnoses, OpenEEG represents a critical step towards trustworthy and clinically deployable EEG-based diagnostic systems.

title: A Novel Dual-Stream Framework for dMRI Tractography Streamline Classification with Joint dMRI and fMRI Data
authors: Haotian Yan, Bocheng Guo, Jianzhong He 0001, Nir A. Sochen, Ofer Pasternak, Lauren J. O'Donnell, Fan Zhang 0013
abstract: Streamline classification is essential to identify anatomically meaningful white matter tracts from diffusion MRI (dMRI) tractography. However, current streamline classification methods rely primarily on the geometric features of the streamline trajectory, failing to distinguish between functionally distinct fiber tracts with similar pathways. To address this, we introduce a novel dual-stream streamline classification framework that jointly analyzes dMRI and functional MRI (fMRI) data to enhance the functional coherence of tract parcellation. We design a novel network that performs streamline classification using a pretrained backbone model for full streamline trajectories, while augmenting with an auxiliary network that processes fMRI signals from fiber endpoint regions. We demonstrate our method by parcellating the corticospinal tract (CST) into its four somatotopic subdivisions. Experimental results from ablation studies and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods demonstrate our approach's superior performance. Code: https://github.com/Hotel-Y/DF-NET_ISBI.git

title: Federated Few-Shot Segmentation for Rare Brain Tumours via Weighted Aggregation and Prototype-Guided Adaptation
authors: Shenghui Yan, Sidong Liu, Maurice Pagnucco, Yang Song 0001
abstract: Brain tumour segmentation is a fundamental task for neurooncological diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the scarcity of annotated data for rarer tumour types such as metastases limits the applicability of deep learning models. Federated learning (FL) enables multi-institutional collaboration without sharing patient data, yet existing approaches struggle with data imbalance, domain heterogeneity, and fewshot generalisation to new centers. We propose a federated framework designed for rare brain tumour segmentation that introduces three key modules: (1) client-specific weighted aggregation to improve fairness and stability under heterogeneous data quality, (2) a cross-attention decoder interaction to enable positive knowledge transfer between tumour types, and (3) a prototype-based decoder initialisation (ProtoInit++) for efficient few-shot adaptation to new centers. Experiments on seven multi-center datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedPer, and FedRep, achieving higher Dice scores and lower Hausdorff distances. Leave-one-center-out evaluations further confirm superior generalisation performance to unseen hospitals.

title: Semi-Supervised Carotid Plaque Segmentation with Multi-Scale Deep Supervision and Consistency Learning for Multi-View Vulnerable Plaque Classification
authors: Long Yang, Xiaoyin Chen, Bing Wang, Pengpeng Ou, Shaomin Niu, Peipei Zhang, Zeping Gao, Teng Ma 0004
abstract: Carotid plaque vulnerability is closely associated with cerebrovascular events, making accurate plaque analysis important for clinical risk assessment. In this study, we propose a framework for automated carotid ultrasound plaque analysis integrating semi-supervised segmentation and classification. A multi-scale deeply supervised dual-view DenseNet model with a UniMatch-based semi-supervised strategy was used for plaque segmentation, enabling effective utilization of labeled and unlabeled data. Radiomic features extracted from plaque, lumen, and union regions were used for vulnerable plaque classification with TabPFN and semi-supervised training. Evaluation on ultrasound examinations yielded a segmentation score of 61.72 and an F1-score of 63.83, with an efficient processing time of 163.54 ms per case (time score: 87.61), securing 7th place overall and demonstrating the potential of our framework for automated plaque analysis.

title: Transformer-Based Foundation Model for Universal Ultrasound Image Analysis
authors: Zhikai Yang, Junjie Hu, Félix Nieto-del-Amor, Guangyuan Li, Rodrigo Moreno
abstract: We propose a transformer-based foundation model for unified multi-task, multi-organ, multi-disease ultrasound image analysis, targeting 27 subtasks across segmentation, classification, detection, and landmark regression. The model follows hard parameter sharing: the encoder of a Swin Transformer pretrained on ImageNet is shared by all tasks, while each task uses its own prediction head. For segmentation and detection tasks, we use feature pyramid network decoders with separate segmentation and detection branches; for classification and regression tasks, we use encoder-level features with specific heads. Compared to other existing methods in offline experiments, the proposed method has the best performance. At the Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC UIA) challenge, our method achieved 8th place among 24th participating teams. The code is public at https://github.com/HJJ-D/Foundation-Model-Challenge-for-Ultrasound-Image-Analysis.

title: DIFF-MAMBA: Efficient State-Space Modeling for End-To-End Ultrasound Video Diagnosis
authors: Jinghan Yang, Tian Jie, Kun Wang
abstract: Breast cancer remains the most common malignancy among women worldwide. B-mode grayscale ultrasound is widely used for screening and diagnosis in dense breast tissue due to its safety, accessibility, and cost-effectiveness. While conventional computeraided diagnostic (CAD) systems rely on static frames, clinical interpretation depends on temporal cues such as probe motion, boundary stability, and posterior acoustic changes. To address this gap, we propose Diff-Mamba, an end-to-end framework that directly processes grayscale ultrasound videos and leverages inter-frame differences to capture motion-consistent structural and textural patterns. Built upon the Mamba selective state-space model, Diff-Mamba efficiently encodes long-range temporal dependencies while preserving temporal continuity. The dual-branch attention pooling module further integrates spatial and temporal information for malignancy prediction. Experiments on two public ultrasound video datasets demonstrate that Diff-Mamba achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing deep learning baselines. The code and dataset resources are publicly available at https://github.com/hanliumu/DIFFMAMBA.

title: UniUltra: A Unified Foundation Model for Universal Ultrasound Analysis
authors: Zi Yang, Zengxing Li, Qingchen Liu, Kun Wang, Yu Fu
abstract: Ultrasound (US) imaging exhibits substantial heterogeneity across anatomical structures, posing significant challenges to the development of generalizable foundation models. In this paper, we present UniUltra, a unified Transformer-based framework designed for the Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC_UIA) 2026. To overcome the resolution bottlenecks and long-range dependency limitations observed in convolutional baselines, our architecture utilizes a Swin V2 Tiny backbone with Log-spaced Continuous Position Bias (Log-CPB) and supports an increased input resolution of$384 \times 384$. We introduce a Single Query Guided Head for classification to adaptively fuse semantic and pixel-level features, and integrate a Differentiable Spatial Numerical Transform (DSNT) layer to achieve subpixel accuracy in biometric regression. Quantitative evaluation across 27 heterogeneous subtasks demonstrates the robustness of our approach, yielding an average Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.8910 in segmentation and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.9313 in classification. Furthermore, the model significantly improves localization precision, attaining a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.7831 in detection and a Mean Radial Error (MRE) of 18.80 in regression. These results validate the efficacy of our Transformer-based multi-task approach in complex clinical ultrasound analysis.

title: Low Performing Pixel Correction in Computed Tomography with Unrolled Network and Synthetic Data Training
authors: Hongxu Yang, Levente Lippenszky, Edina Timko, Lehel Ferenczi, Gopal Avinash
abstract: Low performance pixels (LPP) in Computed Tomography (CT) detectors would lead to ring and streak artifacts in the reconstructed images, making them clinically unusable. In recent years, several solutions have been proposed to correct LPP artifacts, either in the image domain or in the sinogram domain using supervised deep learning methods. However, these methods require dedicated datasets for training, which are expensive to collect. Moreover, existing approaches focus solely either on image-space or sinogram-space correction, ignoring the intrinsic correlations from the forward operation of the CT geometry. In this work, we propose an unrolled dual-domain method based on synthetic data to correct LPP artifacts. Specifically, the intrinsic correlations of LPP between the sinogram and image domains are leveraged through synthetic data generated from natural images, enabling the trained model to correct artifacts without requiring any realworld clinical data. In experiments simulating$1-2 \%$detectors defect near the isocenter, the proposed method outperformed the state-of-the-art approaches by a large margin. The results indicate that our solution can correct LPP artifacts without the cost of data collection for model training, and it is adaptable to different scanner settings for software-based applications.

title: MRI-Based Multi-Scale Multi-Modal Neonatal Brain Age Estimation Framework with Weight-Aware Feature
authors: Zhenyu Yang, Jiakun Xu, Sijin Yu, Ying Ouyang, Xin Zhang
abstract: Accurate assessment of postmenstrual age (PMA) is critical for evaluating neonatal brain development and predicting neurodevelopmental outcomes. This paper presents a novel multi-scale multi-modal MRI framework for neonatal brain age estimation that integrates body weight as a core feature alongside imaging data. Our approach leverages T2-weighted structural MRI (T2w) and fractional anisotropy (FA) of diffusion MRI (dMRI) employing a three-branch network to extract multi-scale anatomical and microstructural features from both modalities. A transformer module then performs weight-aware feature fusion, effectively combining imaging characteristics with clinical weight information for precise PMA prediction. Evaluated on the dHCP neonatal cohort, our method achieves a mean absolute error of 0.48 weeks in term-born infants. Furthermore, our analysis reveals significant brain maturation delays in preterm neonates, the degree of which correlates strongly with both gestational age and body weight. These findings demonstrate the framework's potential as an effective tool for assessing early brain development and identifying deviations from typical maturation trajectories.

title: Semantic-Guided 3D CT Generation for Stroke Lesion Segmentation
authors: Hongxi Yang, Zhen Yu, Deval Mehta 0001, Yasmeen M. George, Zongyuan Ge

title: View-Guided Multi-Task Learning for Fetal Cardiac Segmentation and CHD Classification
authors: Yingyu Yang, Qianye Yang, Can Peng, Yuyuan Liu, J. Alison Noble
abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a major cause of infant morbidity and mortality, and fetal ultrasound is the standard modality for prenatal screening. The FETUS Challenge (ISBI 2026) focuses on the joint tasks of fetal cardiac structure segmentation and CHD-related multi-label classification across standard cardiac views under a semi-supervised learning (SSL) setting. We present a view-guided framework with separate models for segmentation and classification, both augmented with an auxiliary standard-view prediction head. To further exploit anatomical information, we introduce a view-specific geometric classifier that derives explicit geometric features from segmentation masks to capture cardiac structural relationships. On the validation leaderboard, our method (team CHDkiller) achieved an overall score of 52.54 (F1 44.54, DSC 81.34, NSD 63.08), compared with the baseline score of 40.37 (F1 34.20, DSC 65.48, NSD 45.55). On the hidden test leaderboard, CHDkiller obtained an overall score of 47.62 (F1 25.58, DSC 69.85, NSD 46.18), outperforming the baseline score of 36.05 (F1 17.48, DSC 54.11, NSD 33.97), with an inference time of 55.45 ms. Our team ranked 5th on the validation leaderboard and 4th on the hidden test leaderboard. Code available at https://github.com/YingyuYyy/FetalViewGuidedSegCLS.

title: PROZONESAM2: Prostate Zonal Segmentation Using Sam2 and Gland-To-Zones Consistency Constraints
authors: Chunna Yang, Mengting Yang, Zhongwei Zhao, Yan Li, Nengwang Yu, Yipeng Hu, Zhe Min
abstract: Accurate prostate zonal segmentation on MRI is crucial for prostate cancer (PCa) detection and treatment. Traditional CNN-based methods, though effective in single-center training, often lack global context awareness and generalize poorly to external datasets, especially in the peripheral zone (PZ) with fuzzy boundaries. Recently, foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have shown strong segmentation ability, but domain gaps and limited medical annotations hinder their direct use in medical imaging. To address these challenges, we propose ProZoneSAM2, a region-constrained fine-tuning segmentation method built upon SAM2. ProZoneSAM2 fine-tunes only the memory encoder and mask decoder (5.58 M parameters) and introduces a Region-Constrained Loss Mechanism (RCLM) to enforce anatomical consistency among PZ and central gland (CG) by constraining their spatial complementarity within the whole gland (WG). ProZoneSAM2 achieves Dice scores of 94.46%, 92.74 %, and 80.07 % on the internal test (from Prostate158, PROSTATEx, and MSD) and$94.37 \%, 91.91 \%$, and 79.96 % on the external test (NCI-ISBI 2013) for WG, CG, and PZ, outperforming CNN-based and SAM-based methods.

title: Energyflow: A Physically Consistent Learning Framework for 3D Microscopy Deconvolution
authors: Yue Yang, Zhenxuan Zhang, Peiyuan Jing, Krinos Li, Guang Yang 0006
abstract: Three-dimensional fluorescence microscopy images often suffer from blur and noise induced by the point spread function (PSF), leading to loss of resolution and structural fidelity. We propose EnergyFlow, a method for 3D microscopy deconvolution based on energy-guided flow matching. The model learns a restoration flow field along the continuous physical trajectory of degradation, while an energy consistency constraint enforces physical interpretability throughout the degradation-recovery process. This formulation enables image reconstruction without explicit inversion and achieves superior performance over classical deconvolution and deep learning baselines on both synthetic and real fluorescence data. The results demonstrate that energy-guided flow matching provides a robust and physically consistent framework for 3D microscopy restoration.

title: Brain-CLIP: An Individual-Preserving Contrastive Framework for Bidirectional Cross-Modal Brain Connectome Translation
authors: Yaokai Yang, Nan Zhao, Zeyu Zhang, Jing Zhang, Lu Zhang
abstract: Understanding the complex relationship between structural and functional brain networks is essential for uncovering the mechanisms that govern brain organization. However, most existing studies model this relationship in a unidirectional manner, either predicting functional connectivity (FC) from structural connectivity (SC) or vice versa, while very few approaches enable true bidirectional translation between the two modalities. To address this gap, we introduce Brain-CLIP, a novel framework inspired by the multimodal contrastive learning paradigm exemplified by CLIP, in which heterogeneous modalities are aligned in a shared latent space through semantic correspondence. Similarly, Brain-CLIP aligns SC and FC in a common embedding space to achieve bidirectional translation. Furthermore, we propose an Individual-Preserving CLIP Loss that maintains precise subject-level alignment between SC and FC representations, enabling the model to capture individual-specific connectomic patterns rather than merely population-level correspondences. Comprehensive evaluations on two large-scale datasets, HCP and ADNI, demonstrate that Brain-CLIP substantially outperforms existing methods. (Code is available here: https://github.com/BrainX-Lab/Brain-CLIP)

title: Brain-MGF: Multimodal Graph Fusion Network for EEG-FMRI Brain Connectivity Analysis Under Psilocybin
authors: Sin-Yee Yap, Fuad Noman, Junn Yong Loo, Devon Stoliker, Moein Khajehnejad, Raphaël C.-W. Phan, David L. Dowe, Adeel Razi, Chee-Ming Ting
abstract: Psychedelics, such as psilocybin, reorganise large-scale brain connectivity, yet how these changes are reflected across electrophysiological (electroencephalogram, EEG) and haemodynamic (functional magnetic resonance imaging, fMRI) networks remains unclear. We present Brain-MGF, a multimodal graph fusion network for joint EEG-fMRI connectivity analysis. For each modality, we construct graphs with partial-correlation edges and Pearson-profile node features, and learn subject-level embeddings via graph convolution. An adaptive softmax gate then fuses modalities with samplespecific weights to capture context-dependent contributions. Using the world's largest single-site psilocybin dataset, PsiConnect, BrainMGF distinguishes psilocybin condition from no-psilocybin condition in meditation and rest. Fusion improves over unimodal and nonadaptive variants, achieving 74.0% accuracy and 76.5% F1 score on meditation, and 76.0% accuracy with 85.8% ROC-AUC on rest. UMAP visualisations reveal clearer class separation for fused embeddings. These results indicate that adaptive graph fusion effectively integrates complementary EEG-fMRI information, providing an interpretable framework for characterising psilocybin-induced alterations in large-scale neural organisation.

title: DMC-SM: A Fast System Matrix Calibration Method for High-Quality Magnetic Particle Imaging Reconstruction
authors: Jian'an Ye, Ziwei Chen, Gen Shi, Zhongwei Bian, Yu An, Jie Tian 0001
abstract: Magnetic Particle Imaging (MPI) is a novel imaging technique that detects the magnetic response of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles, offering high sensitivity and temporal resolution. However, the system matrix (SM) calibration, which is crucial for quantitative analysis in MPI, remains complex, time-consuming, and prone to artifacts. To address these challenges, we propose a Distance Map Consistent System Matrix (DMC-SM) generation method. By utilizing a one-dimensional distance-domain function, DMC-SM effectively calibrates the system matrix, eliminating distortions and interpolation discontinuities. Specifically, experiments conducted with actual measurement data in closedbore MPI demonstrate that the proposed method enables a larger Field of View (FOV). Additionally, it reduces computational complexity, significantly accelerates calibration speed, and enhances image reconstruction quality. For a$64 \times 64$grid, the system matrix construction time was reduced from 112.64s to just 2.18s, indicating substantial improvements in both speed and efficiency.

title: SAM-TXD: SAM with Text-Guided Diffusion for Refined Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Seunghee Yoo, Junghyo Sohn, Kwanseok Oh, Heung-Il Suk
abstract: While the Segment Anything Model (SAM) has spurred extensive research in medical image segmentation, its direct application to medical images is often suboptimal, struggling with ambiguous boundaries and limited semantic context. We propose SAM-TXD, a diffusion-based framework that refines SAM outputs by conditioning the denoising process on SAM-derived coarse masks and incorporating global and local textual features via a pre-trained CLIP encoder. On QaTa-COV19 and MosMedData+, SAM-TXD achieves 91.33/84.66 and 77.50/64.55 (Dice/mIoU), respectively, surpassing prior methods. Experiments reveal complementary roles: text provides semantic guidance; diffusion resolves ambiguous boundaries and visualizes predictive uncertainty maps; and SAM provides spatial priors. The approach also produces per-pixel uncertainty maps highlighting regions with high inter-observer variability and maintains competitive performance under limited training data. These results demonstrate the promise of integrating diffusion with SAM and multi-level text conditioning for medical image segmentation.

title: PhysHVS-LDCT: Dose-Controllable Physics-Based Low-Dose CT Synthesis for Benchmarking and Data Augmentation
authors: Taifour Yousra, Marouane Tliba, Nour Aburaed, Azeddine Beghdadi, Faouzi Alaya Cheikh, Aladine Chetouani, Zuheng Ming, Rachid Jennane
abstract: Reducing radiation exposure in Computed Tomography (CT) remains a clinical priority, particularly for radiosensitive groups such as pediatric and pregnant patients. Although Low-Dose CT (LDCT) reduces radiation-related risk, lowering the tube current increases noise and artifacts that can compromise diagnostic quality. Progress in LDCT reconstruction is further limited by the scarcity of paired full-dose and low-dose data, as ethical constraints prohibit multi-dose acquisitions. Moreover, most public CT datasets contain only clinical-dose scans, restricting their use for low-dose imaging research. To address this limitation, we introduce a benchmarking-oriented generative framework for synthesizing realistic LDCT images from existing clinical-dose data. We further present PhysHVS-LDCT, a dose-controllable synthesis pipeline designed as an effective dataset augmentation tool. By utilizing both physics-based and perceptual priors informed by human contrast sensitivity, PhysHVS-LDCT produces LDCT images that closely match real low-dose scans. Our results highlight that PhysHVS-LDCT achieves superior performance across all dose levels when compared with SOTA GAN- and VAE-based baselines, producing more accurate and realistic LDCT simulations.

title: DBS-ElecNet: Automated Localization and Segmentation of DBS Electrodes in Clinical MRI
authors: Vanessa H. Yu, Edward Chen, Jürgen Germann, Alexandre Boutet, Andres M. Lozano, Kâmil Uludag, Sriranga Kashyap
abstract: This paper presents DBS-ElecNet, a deep learning framework for automated segmentation of electrodes and artifact regions in post-operative DBS MRI. To overcome reliance on manual annotations, we introduce a hybrid approach where a traditional image processing pipeline generates initial segmentations for the 3D U-Net model, which uses these as ground truth, and achieves robust segmentation performance. DBS-ElecNet performs inference in$\sim 3$seconds, a 60-100x speedup over manual segmentations. This efficient and accurate approach enables scalable analysis for surgical verification and paves the way for advanced clinical applications like artifact inpainting.

title: Boundary-Aware Adversarial Filtering for Reliable Diagnosis Under Extreme Class Imbalance
authors: Yanxuan Yu, Michael S. Hughes, Julien Lee, Jiacheng Zhou, Andrew F. Laine
abstract: We study classification under extreme class imbalance where recall and calibration are both critical: for example, in medical diagnosis scenarios. We propose AF-SMOTE, a mathematically motivated augmentation framework that first synthesizes minority points and then filters them by an adversarial discriminator and a boundary utility model. We prove that, under mild assumptions on the decision boundary smoothness and class-conditional densities, our filtering step monotonically improves a surrogate of$\mathrm{F}_{\beta}$(for$\beta \geq 1$) while not inflating Brier score. On MIMIC-IV proxy label prediction and canonical fraud detection benchmarks, AF-SMOTE attains higher recall and average precision than strong oversampling baselines (SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE, SVM-SMOTE), and yields the best calibration. We further validate these gains across multiple additional datasets beyond MIMIC-IV. Our successful application of AF-SMOTE to a healthcare dataset using a proxy label demonstrates in a disease-agnostic way its practical value in clinical situations, where missing true positive cases in rare diseases can have severe consequences.

title: Entity Knowledge Graph Enhanced Vision Language Model for Multi-Organ Diagnosis
authors: Jianxun Yu, Meirui Jiang, Winnie Chiu Wing Chu, Qi Dou 0001
abstract: Diagnosing diseases from multiple organs is common in clinical practice but remains challenging. This task demands radiologists' implicit understanding of the structural and functional inter-dependencies within organ systems. Incorporating such anatomical ontology knowledge into deep learning models can substantially enhance performance; however, effective strategies for integrating such knowledge with deep learning are not yet well established. To bridge this gap, we propose to encode anatomical ontologies as the entity knowledge graph (EKG) and fuse the graph representations with organ-level 3D CT features for diagnosis. Specifically, we construct the EKG that captures relationships among relevant diseases and organs. This graph is encoded into graph embeddings and further fused with organ-centric patch features via an attention mechanism. By such integration, we can ultimately improve diagnostic accuracy by aligning visual evidence with clinically grounded anatomical priors. We have conducted experiments on a large-scale dataset comprising nine public datasets. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated by significant performance gains over state-of-the-art methods, patient-level diagnostic sensitivity improves by 5.98%, and organ-level sensitivity increases by 10.02%. The code is available at: https://github.com/med-air/EKG-VLM

title: Learning From Limited Multi-Phase CT: Dual-Branch Prototype-Guided Framework for Early Recurrence Prediction in HCC
authors: Hsin-Pei Yu, Si-Qin Lyu, Van Quang Nghiem, Yi-Hsien Hsieh, Weichung Wang, Tung-Hung Su, Jia-Horng Kao, Che Lin
abstract: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is recommended in clinical guidelines for managing hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet complete multi-phase acquisition is often unavailable. Here, we present DuoProto, a novel dualbranch, prototype-guided framework that leverages limited multi-phase CT during training to enhance single-phase ER prediction in HCC. DuoProto aligns class-level representations across single- and multi-phase inputs via prototype learning, incorporates clinically informed ranking, and infers with single-phase only. Under conditions of class imbalance and missing phase, DuoProto consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving absolute gains of$3-9 \%$across all metrics. The proposed framework provides a clinically aligned solution, enabling more informed decision-making. Code is available at https://github.com/idssplab/DuoProto.

title: CoPrimeEEG: CRT-Guided Dual-Branch Reconstruction from Co-Prime Sub-Nyquist EEG
authors: Yanxuan Yu, Dong Liu 0049, Ying Nian Wu
abstract: We present CoPrimeEEG, a neural reconstruction framework that unifies co-prime sub-Nyquist sampling theory with a CRT-guided learning objective for EEG. Two low-rate streams obtained by co-prime decimations feed a dual-branch convolutional encoder whose fused representation is upsampled to reconstruct high-rate EEG while jointly predicting a temporal usefulness mask and canonical bandpower features. We derive a principled loss with four terms: (i) waveform fidelity, (ii) mask sparsity and smoothness, (iii) bandpower supervision in the log-domain, and (iv) a CRT-consistency term enforcing agreement between the reconstruction and its co-prime downsampled counterparts. On real EEG data, CoPrimeEEG achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality across MSE, MAE, correlation, SNR, and PSNR while using fewer parameters. The approach provides a practical path to low-power EEG acquisition with high-fidelity downstream analysis.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Structured Data Extraction from Full CMR Reports via Distilled LLMS
authors: Yi Yu, Parker Martin, Zhenyu Bu, Yixuan Liu, Yi-Yu Zheng, Orlando P. Simonetti, Yuchi Han, Yuan Xue 0002
abstract: Converting free-text cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) reports into auditable structured data remains a bottleneck for cohort assembly, longitudinal curation, and clinical decision support. We present CMR-EXTR, a lightweight framework that converts free-text CMR reports into structured data and assigns per-field confidence for quality control. A teacher-student distillation pipeline enables fully offline inference while limiting manual annotation. Uncertainty integrates three complementary principles-distribution plausibility, sampling stability, and cross-field consistency-to triage human review. Experiments show that CMR-EXTR achieves 99.65 % variable-level accuracy, demonstrating both reliable extraction and informative confidence scores. To our knowledge, this is the first CMR-specific extraction system with integrated confidence estimation. The code is available at https://github.com/yuyi1005/CMR-EXTR.

title: A Multi-Modal Transformer for Ultrasound-Guided Diffuse Optical Tomography
authors: Seongkwon Yu, SeokHwan Oh, Yuqing Liang, Jimin Lee, Bumjun Koh, Hyeon-Min Bae
abstract: Diffuse Optical Tomography (DOT) is a non-invasive imaging modality that estimates tissue optical properties using near-infrared (NIR) light. Conventional DOT reconstruction methods suffer from poor spatial resolution and instability due to the ill-posed inverse problem. In this work, we propose MDOT-former, a multi-modal transformer that integrates B-mode ultrasound (US) imaging with DOT to enhance reconstruction accuracy. The proposed model employs a multimodal cross-attention transformer to extract morphological features from US images and improve the localization and quantification of optical properties. To facilitate model training, we introduce an in-silico simulation framework that synthesizes paired DOT and US data. We evaluate MDOT-former using both in-silico and ex-vivo experiments, demonstrating a significant improvement over state-of-the-art (SOTA) learning-based algorithms. MDOT-former achieves 95% lesion identification sensitivity and improves both structural and quantitative accuracy in lesion detection. The results highlight the potential of multi-modal deep learning in advancing DOT reconstruction for biomedical imaging applications.

title: Trialign: Pathology-Aware a $\beta$-Pet Synthesis From MRI via Disentangled Anatomical, Pathological, and Modality Alignment
authors: Hongjie Yu, Kaicong Sun, Dinggang Shen
abstract: Detection of Amyloid-$\beta$($\mathrm{A} \beta$) deposition is critical for timely diagnosis and intervention in Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Although$\mathrm{A} \beta$-Positron Emission Tomography ($\mathrm{A} \beta$-PET) enables in vivo visualization of$\mathrm{A} \beta$pathology, its limited accessibility hinders routine clinical use. In contrast, T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (T1w-MRI) is widely available but lacks pathological sensitivity. Recent MRI-to-PET synthesis methods intend to bridge this gap. Still, they often overemphasize anatomical differences and fail to capture pathology-specific signals due to incomplete disentanglement of anatomical, pathological, and modality alignments. To address this, we propose TriAlign, a two-stage$\mathrm{A} \beta$-PET synthesis framework that explicitly decouples these three alignments. In the first stage, a multimodal variational autoencoder enforces latent consistency between complete and PET-masked MRI-PET pairs, capturing anatomical and A$\beta$-related pathological features. Meanwhile, the decoder ensures modality alignment through$\mathrm{A} \beta$-PET reconstruction. In the second stage, a pathology-aware latent diffusion model refines pathology-specific residual between latent features of complete and masked MRI-PET pairs, guided by multi-scale anatomical cues and demographic prompts. Experiments demonstrate that TriAlign outperforms three widely used models in terms of image quality and$\mathrm{A} \beta$status classification.

title: Artifact Correction and Quality Assessment via Perceptual Contrastive Learning on Diffusion MRI
authors: Jiahao Yu, Tenglong Wang, Yu Xie, Jiaolong Qin, Ye Wu 0001
abstract: Diffusion MRI is crucial for examining the microstructure of brain tissues, which are often affected by artifacts such as ghosting and motion distortions that hinder analysis. This work proposes a novel framework for joint artifact correction and quality assessment based on perceptual contrast. This framework integrates two stages of artifact correction and no-reference quality evaluation at the 3D layer level. In the first stage, we utilize an enhanced 3D U-Net architecture with Leaky ReLU activation and trilinear up-sampling. A hybrid perceptual loss function combining NMAE and HaarPSI is employed to effectively correct artifacts across 4D DWI data, yielding high-fidelity images. In the second stage, we construct a pseudo-reference by extracting low-level voxel-level similarity features and high-level perceptual features from the pre- and post-corrected data. Support Vector Machine techniques are applied to accurately classify images as artifact-laden or artifact-free, facilitating no-reference quality assessment. Our framework exhibits exceptional robustness across diverse acquisition protocols, outperforming existing methods and demonstrating superior artifact-correction capabilities. This research presents a reliable technical framework for automated quality control in dMRI, providing a strong foundation for subsequent clinical quantitative analyses. The code is available at https://github.com/yjh200319/React-QC_Artifact_Correction_Quality_Assessment_On_dMRI.

title: LIDSS: A Latent Information-Driven Dynamic Framework for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Yuan Yuan, Deping Zhang, Bingfeng Luo, Yaozhong Luo, Shaopeng Liu, Xu Lu
abstract: Semi-supervised learning has emerged as a promising approach to address the challenge of scarce high-quality annotations in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. However, existing methods often suffer from limited segmentation accuracy due to difficulties in effectively leveraging labeled data, which stems from low tissue contrast, ambiguous anatomical boundaries, and a lack of reliable supervision in unlabeled regions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel latent information-driven dynamic semi-supervised segmentation (LIDSS) framework. LIDSS incorporates three key components: an enhanced boundary refinement module (EBRM) to improve discriminative feature extraction along tissue borders, a confidence-guided adaptive replacement module (CGAR) that enhances feature learning robustness through an adaptive fusion mechanism, and a self-contrasting auxiliary training strategy to minimize discrepancies between dual decoders. Extensive experiments on the PROMISE12 and ACDC benchmark datasets demonstrate that LIDSS achieves superior segmentation accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation methods.

title: Strict Quadratically-Constrained Parallel Transmit Design with Unrolled Homeomorphic Projection
authors: Junno Yun, Toygan Kilic, Jürgen Herrler, Patrick Liebig, Kâmil Ugurbil, Mehmet Akçakaya
abstract: Parallel transmission (pTx) has been widely adopted to mitigate transmit field ($\mathrm{B}_{1}^{+}$) inhomogeneities in ultrahigh field (UHF) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). pTx design optimizes subject-specific radiofrequency (RF) pulses under strict quadratic constraints for specific absorption rate (SAR) and power. Deep learning-based pTx design has received attention due to its ultrafast processing times compared to conventional optimization methods, but the incorporation of strict quadratic constratints has remained a challenge. In this work, we present an end-to-end deep learning framework for pTx design that explicitly enforces quadratic SAR constraints through an unrolled homeomorphic projection method. The proposed approach guarantees that neural network outputs strictly comply with RF safety limits, while achieving accurate and homogeneous flip angle maps without any postprocessing, substantially reducing computation time.

title: MFD: Modality-Aware Fusion of FMRI and MEG for Noninvasive Speech Decoding
authors: Pengfei Yun, Che Liu, Changde Du, Huiguang He, Dinggang Shen
abstract: Restoring speech from noninvasive brain signals is crucial for practical language brain-computer interfaces and understanding cortical language representation. However, noninvasive recordings still face a fundamental spatial-temporal trade-off: functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) provides fine spatial localization but slow hemodynamics, whereas magnetoencephalography (MEG) captures rapid neural dynamics with lower spatial resolution. To boost decoding accuracy, we exploit their complementarity and propose MFD, a modalityaware, two-stage fusion framework for continuous Mandarin speech decoding. MFD adaptively integrates fMRI and MEG representations, enabling cross-modal compensation between spatial and temporal features. Results on a public multimodal Mandarin dataset show that MFD consistently outperforms unimodal baselines in retrieval tasks, achieving 61.7 % top10 accuracy among 553 candidates. Further analysis indicates MEG representations better capture temporal-acoustic structure, while fMRI correlates more strongly with semantic content. These results highlight the complementary nature of fMRI and MEG and demonstrate the potential of multimodal fusion frameworks for neural speech decoding.

title: BVD: A Two-Stage Network for Identifying Bronchial Variation Types from CT Images
authors: Chang Yuwen, Xuelian Cheng, Junrong Yang, Xin Wang 0094, Juxi Leitner, Zongyuan Ge
abstract: Accurate identification of bronchial variation (BV) types is essential for pulmonary surgery planning and anatomical studies, but current approaches still rely heavily on manual assessment. This paper introduces the Bronchial Variations Detector (BVD), the first automated framework that associates bronchial bifurcation keypoints with BV type classification using CT images. The proposed two-stage pipeline first detects key bifurcation points via SCN-based heatmap regression and then classifies BV types using Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Logistic Regression (LR) based on Euclidean distances along the bronchial skeleton. We curated a multi-center dataset comprising 718 CT scans annotated with 20 key bifurcation points and their variant types. Experimental results show that BVD accurately identifies bronchial variation patterns, highlighting its potential for bronchoscopic navigation and personalized surgical planning. The code and dataset will be publicly available after publication.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Five Hippocampal Segmentation Algorithms in Limbic Encephalitis: Addressing Inflammation and Atrophy Challenges
authors: Walaa Zakaria, Alae Eddine El Barkaoui, Guillaume Criton, Jérôme Honnorat, François Cotton, Bastien Joubert, Thomas Grenier

title: SFNet: Spatial-Frequency Collaborative Network for Fast System Matrix Calibration in Magnetic Particle Imaging
authors: Penghua Zhai, Weixin Xu, Ao Xiao, Xinran Jiang, Jie Tian 0001, Wei Mu
abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a promising high-resolution molecular imaging technology that reconstructs images using system matrix (SM) describing the nonlinear response of magnetic nanoparticles excited along the field-free region (FFR) trajectory. Given SM is required whenever scan parameters or tracer changes, fast SM calibration is important in practical deployment. While sparse sampling enables fast reconstruction without a full-size SM, the predefined sampling grid often misaligns with FFR trajectory. This misalignment leads to incomplete and spatially inconsistent signal acquisition, resulting in SM distortion in both spatial-domain and frequency-domain and consequently introducing structural degradation and artifacts in reconstructed images. Here, we propose a spatial-frequency collaborative network (SFNet), which comprises a frequency-domain feature extraction module and a spatial-frequency feature interaction module. These modules are iteratively optimized to enhance cross-domain representation learning, thereby correcting SM distortion and improving reconstruction fidelity. Experimental results show that the outstanding performance of SFNet against state-of-the-art methods.

title: Segmentation and Diagnosis of Fetal Heart Ultrasound Based on Anatomical Structure Priors and Dual-Threshold Guided Semi-Supervised Learning
authors: Bo Zhai, Changqin Yan, Zhiyuan Zhao, Fangjin Deng, Feng Wei, Chenzi Wang, Kundong Mo
abstract: Aiming at the problems of scarce labeled data, complex anatomical structures and insufficient boundary accuracy in intelligent diagnosis of fetal congenital heart disease, this paper proposes a fetal heart ultrasound segmentation and diagnosis algorithm fusing anatomical structure prior and semi-supervised learning. Its innovations include three aspects: designing an Anatomical Structure Query-based Segmentation Decoder to embed medical prior into global feature learning; proposing a View-Aware Connected Component Loss to dynamically constrain the connected domain morphology of anatomical structures and suppress false positives and structural fragmentation; putting forward a Dual-Threshold Guided Semi-Supervised Classification Learning strategy to maximize the value of unlabeled data and alleviate class imbalance and pseudo-label noise. Ablation studies on the FETUS 2026 dataset reveal that our modular framework achieves state-of-the-art performance by specializing components: the Anatomical Structure Query Decoder drives segmentation accuracy with a DSC of 74.43 and an NSD of 49.16, whereas the View-Aware Connected Component Loss optimizes the comprehensive diagnostic metric with an overall Score of 48.17, collectively demonstrating superior generalization and robustness compared to the baseline.

title: Hospital-Specific Bias in Patch-Based Pathology Models
authors: Mengliang Zhang
abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) achieve strong performance on diverse histopathology tasks, but their sensitivity to hospital-specific domain shifts remains underexplored. We systematically evaluate state-of-the-art PFMs on TCGA patch-level datasets and introduce a lightweight adversarial adaptor to remove hospital-related domain information from latent representations. Experiments show that, while disease classification accuracy is largely maintained, the adaptor effectively reduces hospital-specific bias, as confirmed by t-SNE visualizations. Our study establishes a benchmark for assessing cross-hospital robustness in PFMs and provides a practical strategy for enhancing generalization under heterogeneous clinical settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/MengRes/pfm_domain_bias.

title: Cross-Attention Fusion of Structural and Deformation-Based Mri Features for Alzheimer's Disease Classification
authors: Shijia Zhang, Xiyu Ding, Brian Caffo, Junyu Chen, Xinyi Zhang, Hadi Kharrazi, Zheyu Wang
abstract: Accurate assessment of Alzheimer's disease (AD) using neuroimaging is important for understanding disease progression and supporting clinical research. Structural MRI (sMRI) is widely used for this purpose, but most deep learning approaches primarily rely on intensity-based features, which may not fully capture subtle morphological variations. Jacobian determinant maps (JSM) provide complementary information by describing localized brain deformations; however, conventional multimodal fusion strategies such as early or late fusion may not fully capture the interactions between these modalities. To address this, we explore a cross-attention fusion approach that explicitly models the relationship between sMRI intensity and JSM-derived deformation features for AD classification. Using data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we compare cross-attention with pairwise self-attention and four baseline fusion methods. The proposed approach achieved mean ROC-AUC scores of 0.903 (0.033) for AD vs. cognitively normal (CN) and 0.692 (0.061) for mild cognitive impairment (MCI) vs. CN under five-fold cross-validation. The proposed approach achieved the best performance among fusion strategies and achieved higher or comparable performance with only 1.56 million parameters. These findings suggest that cross-attention fusion may serve as a potentially useful approach for integrating structural and deformation-based MRI features in AD classification tasks.

title: Cortical Surface-Constrained Temporally Continuous Atlas Learning for Fetal Brain MRI
authors: Kai Zhang 0039, Dan Hu 0004, Jiale Cheng, Shijie Huang, Weili Lin, Dinggang Shen, Gang Li 0001
abstract: Constructing a temporally continuous fetal brain atlas with anatomically realistic cortical geometry remains challenging due to rapid cortical folding during gestation. Deep learning, especially Implicit Neural Representation (INR) based methods, improves continuity but often fails to ensure cortical alignment due to the absence of explicit geometric constraints. We propose a cortical surface-constrained joint learning framework that integrates a registration network with an INR for continuous atlas representation. The registration network learns accurate deformation fields, while surface constraints guide alignment to preserve cortical topology. Through joint optimization, our method constructs a temporally continuous fetal brain atlas that captures smooth developmental transitions and preserves anatomically faithful cortical folding. Experiments on the dHCP dataset demonstrate that our method produces anatomically consistent and temporally smooth 4D atlases, achieving superior label-propagation (atlas-based) segmentation accuracy and biologically plausible developmental trajectories.

title: FMIR, A Foundation Model-Based Image Registration Framework for Robust Image Registration
authors: Fengting Zhang, Yue He 0003, Qinghao Liu, Yaonan Wang 0001, Xiang Chen 0008, Hang Zhang 0010
abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized medical image registration by achieving unprecedented speeds, yet its clinical application is hindered by a limited ability to generalize beyond the training domain, a critical weakness given the typically small scale of medical datasets. In this paper, we introduce FMIR, a foundation model-based registration framework that overcomes this limitation. Combining a foundation model-based feature encoder for extracting anatomical structures with a general registration head, and trained with a channel regularization strategy on just a single dataset, FMIR achieves state-of-the-art(SOTA) in-domain performance while maintaining robust registration on out-of-domain images. Our approach demonstrates a viable path toward building generalizable medical imaging foundation models with limited resources. The source code will be released upon acceptance.

title: Pretext Task Adversarial Learning for Unpaired Low-Field to Ultra High-Field MRI Synthesis
authors: Zhenxuan Zhang, Peiyuan Jing, Zi Wang 0005, Ula Briski, Coraline Beitone, Yue Yang, Yinzhe Wu 0001, Fanwen Wang, Liutao Yang, Jiahao Huang, Zhifan Gao, Guang Yang 0006, Peter J. Lally
abstract: Given the scarcity and high cost of high-field MRI, synthesizing high-field images from low-field MRI offers great potential for augmenting limited data in downstream tasks (e.g., segmentation). Low-field MRI typically suffers from low SNR and spatial resolution, making cross-domain synthesis challenging due to feature misalignment and anatomical distortion. To address this, we propose a Pretext Task Adversarial (PTA) framework for high-field MRI synthesis. It consists of: (1) a Slice-wise Gap Perception (SGP) network for aligning inter-slice inconsistencies via contrastive learning; (2) a Local Structure Correction (LSC) network for refining local details from rotated and masked inputs; and (3) a pretext-guided adversarial training that enhances realism through additional supervision and discrimination. Experiments on low-to-ultra-high-field MRI demonstrate state-of-the-art performance (FID =16.892, IS =1.933, MS-SSIM =0.324), generating anatomically consistent high-field-like data to improve downstream training. The code is available at: https://github.com/Zhenxuan-Zhang/PTA4Unpaired_HF_MRI_SYN.

title: Log Focal Frequency Loss for Bioimage Restoration
authors: Xingjian Zhang, Claire Leclech, Louison Blivet-Bailly, Abdul I. Barakat, Elsa D. Angelini
abstract: Image restoration of biological structures in microscopy poses unique challenges for preserving fine textures and sharp edges. While recent GAN-based image restoration formulations have introduced frequency-domain losses for natural images, microscopy images pose distinct challenges with large dynamic ranges and sparse but critical structures with spatially-variable contrast. Inspired by the principle of logarithmic perception in human vision, we propose a log focal frequency loss (LFFL) tailored for microscopy restoration. This loss combines adaptive spectral weighting from log-space differences with log-dampened error measurement, ensuring balanced reconstruction across all frequency bands while preserving both structural coherence and fine details. We tested our GAN-based framework on two use-cases with real ground-truths: deblurring of fluorescence images of cell nuclei on microgroove substrates and denoising of zebrafish embryo images from the FMD dataset. Compared to training with only spatial-domain losses and with existing frequencydomain losses, our method achieves improvements across several quality metrics. Code is available at github.com/xjzhaang/log-focal-frequency-loss.

title: Integrating Population and Individual Brain Network with Mixture-of-Experts for Mild Cognitive Impairment Study
authors: Jing Zhang 0010, Yanjun Lyu, Chao Cao, Minheng Chen, Tong Chen, Li Su, Tianming Liu 0001, Dajiang Zhu
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) diagnosis from neuroimaging requires a comprehensive understanding of brain connectivity patterns. While multi-atlas approaches provide complementary perspectives on brain organization, existing methods rely predominantly on functional connectivity and employ static fusion strategies that introduce information redundancy. To address this, we propose a novel framework that integrates individualized three-hinge gyrus (3 HG) -based brain networks with population-level atlases based networks through a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture. Specifically, brain graph encoders extract structural and functional connectivity embeddings from each atlas, which are processed by atlas-shared and atlas-specific experts to learn atlas-shared and atlas-specific brain patterns, respectively. A gating mechanism dynamically weighs expert contributions, enabling adaptive cross-atlas fusion. Evaluations on the ADNI demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance while providing interpretable insights into atlas-specific diagnostic contributions. Code is available at: https://github.com/Nancy-Zhang-0/Multi-Atlas-MoE

title: Sam-Peft: a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Framework Fusing Multi-Modal Mri for Prompt-Free Glioma Segmentation
authors: Wenkai Zhang, Jie Liu, Fengbin Jin, Jianan Cui, Yuanjing Feng
abstract: Accurate glioma delineation on multi-modal MRI is pivotal for clinical planning, yet remains difficult in practice: cross-site fusion of T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR is brittle, routine pipelines lack manual point/box prompts, and fully fine-tuning large backbones is compute-intensive. In this paper, we present SAM-PEFT, a promptfree, parameter-efficient adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for multi-modal MRI glioma segmentation. SAM-PEFT freezes the SAM backbone and adds: (i) a Multi-Modal Feature Adaptive Fusion (MFAM) for T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR integration; (ii) a Lightweight Prompt Encoder (LPE) with efficient anatomical positional encoding to generate dense internal prompts; and (iii) TransMedAttention for fine-grained refinement. Training only$\sim 5.8 \%$of the model parameters, SAM-PEFT attains a mean Dice of 0.9151 on a held-out test split of the BraTS 2025 preoperative subset, matching or exceeding strong CNN/Transformer baselines and SAM variants. These results suggest a practical route to adapt foundation models to clinical MRI segmentation with modest compute.

title: Lost in Distortion: Uncovering the Domain Gap Between Computer Vision and Brain Imaging - a Study on Pretraining for Age Prediction
authors: Yanteng Zhang, Songheng Li, Zeyu Shen, Qizhen Lan, Lipei Zhang, Yang Liu, Vince D. Calhoun
abstract: Large-scale brain imaging datasets provide unprecedented opportunities for developing domain foundation models through pretraining. However, unlike natural image datasets in computer vision, these neuroimaging data often exhibit high heterogeneity in quality, ranging from well-structured scans to severely distorted or incomplete brain volumes. This raises a fundamental question: can noise or low-quality scans contribute meaningfully to pretraining, or do they instead hinder model learning? In this study, we systematically explore the role of data quality level in pretraining and its impact on downstream tasks. Specifically, we perform pretraining on datasets with different quality levels and perform fine-tuning for brain age prediction on external cohorts. Our results show significant performance differences across quality levels, revealing both opportunities and limitations. We further discuss the gap between computer vision practices and clinical neuroimaging standards, emphasizing the necessity of domain-aware curation to ensure trusted and generalizable domain-specific foundation models.

title: Two-Stage Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Quantitative MRI with Diffusion-Based Refinement for Synthetic DIR Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis
authors: Bin Zhang, Xingyang Wu, Dong Liang 0001, Yihang Zhou, Haifeng Wang 0003
abstract: Quantitative mapping and double inversion recovery (DIR) imaging enhance lesion visibility in multiple sclerosis (MS) but are limited by long, non-routine acquisition times. We propose a physics-guided self-supervised framework to estimate T1, T2, and PD maps directly from standard clinical scans (T1w, T2w, and FLAIR). Stage 1 utilizes a conditional GAN to generate pseudo-quantitative maps constrained by Bloch-based forward modeling, enabling training without paired labels. Stage 2 leverages these pseudo-labels to learn a conditional diffusion prior, followed by physics-consistency posterior sampling to derive high-fidelity quantitative maps. Evaluation on 50 MS patients demonstrates that our twostage approach significantly outperforms GAN-only baselines, achieving up to +28 dB PSNR gain and near-perfect structural agreement (SSIM$\approx 0.999$). The refined maps enable high-quality DIR synthesis with superior cortical lesion visibility, offering a practical, acquisition-free strategy for quantitative MRI within routine clinical protocols.

title: Task-Oriented Uncertainty Collaborative Learning for Label-Efficient Brain Tumor Segmentation
authors: Zhenxuan Zhang, Hongjie Wu, Tao Wang 0085, Jiahao Huang, Baihong Xie, Zhifan Gao, Peter J. Lally, Guang Yang 0006
abstract: Multi-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enhances brain tumour segmentation by combining complementary tissue information from different contrasts. Yet, existing approaches struggle with multi-level specificity perception and data heterogeneity, particularly under limited annotations. We propose a Task-oriented Uncertainty Collaborative Learning (TUCL) framework that integrates a task-oriented prompt attention (TPA) module and a dual-path uncertainty refinement (DUR) strategy for robust multi-contrast segmentation. TPA employs intra- and cross-prompt attention to model inter-contrast dependencies, while DUR iteratively refines predictions through uncertainty feedback. Evaluated on limited-label MRI data, TUCL achieves a Dice score of 88.2 % and HD95 of 10.853 mm, demonstrating strong generalisation and reduced reliance on extensive annotations. Code: https://github.com/Zhenxuan-Zhang/TUCL_BrainSeg

title: BEFNet: Boundary-Enhanced Fusion Network for Early Esophageal Cancer Segmentation
authors: Lei Zhang, Zihuang Wu, Xinyu Xiong, Ming Li 0042, Guanbin Li
abstract: Accurate segmentation of Early Esophageal Cancer (EEC) lesions is critical for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. However, this task remains challenging due to the poorly defined boundaries of such lesions. To address this issue, we propose BEFNet, a novel segmentation network tailored for EEC. The main contributions of this work are threefold: (1) We design a Boundary Enhancement Module (BEM) that extracts and refines ambiguous lesion boundaries from multiscale backbone features. (2) We introduce a Dynamic Focusing and Mining Module (DFMM) to hierarchically integrate encoder features at different stages, effectively mitigating the semantic gap between shallow and deep layers. (3) We develop a Boundary-aware Contextual Attention Module (BCAM) to comprehensively fuse all decoder features with boundary priors for precise final prediction. Extensive experiments on a challenging public EEC dataset demonstrate that BEFNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing recent leading methods.

title: SFENet: Shallow Feature Excitation for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
authors: Lei Zhang, Zihuang Wu, Xinyu Xiong, Ming Li 0042, Guanbin Li
abstract: Retinal vessel segmentation is crucial for ophthalmic diagnosis, yet deploying deep learning models on mobile devices remains challenging due to high computational complexity. We propose a lightweight framework, SFENet, that achieves accurate segmentation with minimal resource requirements. Unlike traditional U-Net-based models that rely on deep, computationally intensive encoders, SFENet employs a streamlined single-branch architecture and emphasizes shallow features. Its core innovations include three modules: a hierarchical receptive field module (HRFM) for efficient multi-scale feature extraction, a feature refinement module (FRM) for enhancing vessel detail through dual-branch fusion, and a spatial context mining module (SCMM) for modeling long-range dependencies to ensure vessel continuity. This design significantly reduces model parameters and inference time while maintaining high accuracy, making SFENet suitable for real-time applications on edge devices. Experiments on multiple public datasets confirm that SFENet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Towards Universal Ultrasound Analysis: Parameter-Efficient Foundation Model With Task-Aware Routing for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Learning
authors: Yixuan Zhang 0006, Qing Xu 0014, Yue Li, Xiangjian He, Zhen Chen 0013
abstract: Developing a universal foundation model for ultrasound imaging is inherently challenging due to severe speckle noise, diverse acquisition protocols, and the semantic gap between heterogeneous clinical tasks. Traditional multi-task learning often suffers from negative transfer when simultaneously optimizing dense (i.e., segmentation, detection) and global (i.e., classification, regression) predictions. In this paper, we propose UltraTAR, a parameter-efficient Task-Aware Routing framework that won 1st Place in the Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC-UIA) 2026. Instead of full fine-tuning, we leverage a frozen Vision Foundation Model (VFM) adapted via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to preserve robust pre-trained representations while injecting lightweight task-specific knowledge. To overcome the architectural disconnect between single-scale foundation features and diverse task requirements, we design a task-aware dual-branch routing strategy, including a novel Feature Pyramid Adapter that constructs hierarchical FPN-compatible representations for dense tasks, and a CLS-guided feature fusion module that enriches global context for diagnostic tasks. Furthermore, an anchorfree CenterNet head and empirical loss scaling are integrated to harmonize optimization across 27 distinct subtasks. Evaluated on the large-scale FMC-UIA 2026 benchmark, our UltraTAR establishes a new state-of-the-art, outperforming the official baseline by large margins (e.g.,$+189 \%$in Detection IoU and$+19 \%$in Segmentation DSC) and demonstrating exceptional versatility for universal ultrasound analysis.

title: Freqdino: Frequency-Guided Adaptation for Generalized Boundary-Aware Ultrasound Image Segmentation
authors: Yixuan Zhang 0006, Qing Xu 0014, Yue Li, Xiangjian He, Qian Zhang 0018, Mainul Haque, Rong Qu, Wenting Duan, Zhen Chen 0013
abstract: Ultrasound image segmentation is pivotal for clinical diagnosis, yet challenged by speckle noise and imaging artifacts. Recently, DINOv3 has shown remarkable promise in medical image segmentation with its powerful representation capabilities. However, DINOv3, pre-trained on natural images, lacks sensitivity to ultrasound-specific boundary degradation. To address this limitation, we propose FreqDINO, a frequency-guided segmentation framework that enhances boundary perception and structural consistency. Specifically, we devise a Multi-scale Frequency Extraction and Alignment (MFEA) strategy to separate low-frequency structures and multi-scale high-frequency boundary details, and align them via learnable attention. We also introduce a Frequency-Guided Boundary Refinement (FGBR) module that extracts boundary prototypes from high-frequency components and refines spatial features. Furthermore, we design a Multi-task Boundary-Guided Decoder (MBGD) to ensure spatial coherence between boundary and semantic predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FreqDINO surpasses state-of-the-art methods with superior achieves remarkable generalization capability. The code is available at https://github.com/MingLang-FD/FreqDINO.

title: AutoATQ: Automating Along-Tract Quantification Without Tractography
authors: Chengzhe Zhang, Yu Xie, Zhonghua Wan 0002, Tenglong Wang, Ye Wu
abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) is a unique noninvasive technique for characterizing brain white-matter microstructure, and tractometry is a key analytical method for identifying localized abnormalities. However, traditional tractometry relies on tractography, which has significant limitations, including indirect inference of anatomy, false-positive streamlines, and difficulties with crossing fibers. Additionally, it requires a lengthy acquisition of$q$-space data. To this end, we propose a novel deep learning framework for direct microstructural characterization using white matter bundle masks, thereby eliminating the need for tractography. Our approach uses the U-Mamba network to accurately segment 72 predefined white matter bundles from parameterized spherical mean images, thereby enhancing tissue specificity. We also introduce a dedicated point cloud network to estimate the centerline of each tract and aggregate voxel-wise microstructural features for detailed analysis. Experimental results show that our framework's profiles align closely with those from the established along-tract analytics. Ultimately, we offer a more robust and efficient tractometric solution that advances the clinical use of dMRI and facilitates large-scale neuroimaging studies. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Zhang-Chengzhe/AutoATQ.

title: Toward Achieving Adjustable Smoothing Level in Cardiac-Gated SPECT Studies with a Deep Learning Denoising Network
authors: Xirang Zhang, Yongyi Yang, Jovan G. Brankov, Michael A. King

title: Multi-Modal Domain Adaptation for Cancer Diagnosis via Integration of Pathological Images and Clinical Text Data
authors: Binyu Zhang, Kai Yang, Wei Shao
abstract: Whole-slide pathological images (WSIs) have long been regarded as the gold standard for cancer diagnosis and treatment planning. Recent research shows that the integrative analysis of WSIs with their corresponding pathological reports can significantly enhance diagnostic accuracy, as it leverages complementary visual-textual cues. However, data from different centers often have notable distribution shifts that hinder model adaptation across different sites. To solve this problem, we propose$\mathrm{M}^{2} \text{DA}$-ICT (Multi-modal Domain Adaptation via Integration of Pathological Images and Clinical Texts), a new framework for enhancing cross-center cancer diagnosis. Specifically, for the pathological images, we introduce a graph-based topology alignment module, which represents each WSI as a patch-level graph and aligns domain distributions using Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) on both node and topological features. For the clinical text data, we utilize embeddings derived from pretrained vision-language models to perform distribution alignment between source and target centers via MMD. Finally, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) module is adopted to combine the pathological image and text reports data to conduct cancer diagnosis. Extensive experiments on TCGA-BRCA and TCGA-KIRC datasets show M²DA-ICT consistently outperforms the existing multimodal domain adaptation baselines.

title: Disdiff: Self-Supervised Segmentation on Histopathology Images Using Diffusion Models and Distance Maps
authors: Xuanke Zhang, Qi Zhang, Jia Gu, Runyang Jian, Chongyu Bao, Ziyang Zhu, Fengyong You, Jingzhang Sun
abstract: Histopathological image segmentation is crucial for clinical diagnosis, but obtaining high-quality annotations is timeconsuming and labor-intensive. To improve segmentation performance while reducing annotation dependence, this paper presents DisDiff, a novel two-stage self-supervised framework leveraging diffusion models for nuclei segmentation without pseudo-labels. In the first stage, a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) with Perception Prioritized (P2) weighting learns robust features from unlabeled images. In the second stage, pretrained weights are transferred to a U-Net enhanced with Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA) and distance map post-processing for effective nuclei separation. Experiments on TCGA and TNBC datasets show that DisDiff achieves competitive performance with only 50 % labeled data and superior results with full annotations, demonstrating practical value for clinical applications.

title: Foundation Model-Guided Iteratively Prompting and Pseudo-Labeling for Partially Labeled Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Qiaochu Zhao, Wei Wei, David Horowitz, Richard Bakst, Yading Yuan
abstract: Automated medical image segmentation has achieved remarkable progress with fully labeled data. However, sitespecific clinical priorities and the high cost of manual annotation often yield scans with only a subset of organs labeled, leading to the partially labeled problem that degrades performance. To address this issue, we propose IPnP, an Iteratively Prompting and Pseudo-labeling framework, for partially labeled medical image segmentation. IPnP iteratively generates and refines pseudo-labels for unlabeled organs through collaboration between a trainable segmentation network (specialist) and a frozen foundation model (generalist), progressively recovering full-organ supervision. On the public dataset AMOS with the simulated partial-label setting, IPnP consistently improves segmentation performance over prior methods and approaches the performance of the fully labeled reference. We further evaluate on a private, partially labeled dataset of 210 head-and-neck cancer patients and demonstrate our effectiveness in real-world clinical settings.

title: 3D DoseGLA: Gated Linear Attention with Wavelet-Domain Constraint for Efficient 3D Radiotherapy Dose Prediction
authors: Ku Zhao, Xianhao Zhou, Wenjun Liao, Shichuan Zhang, Shaoting Zhang 0001, Guotai Wang
abstract: Dose calculation, as the core of radiotherapy, remains a timeconsuming and experience-dependent process. While deep learning methods have been proposed to improve efficiency, they often face challenges in global modeling and computational complexity, especially with 3D data, limiting their clinical applicability. Moreover, their predicted dose maps are often over-smoothed due to pixel-wise loss functions such as L1 loss that ignore inter-pixel relationship. To address these issues, we propose an efficient framework DoseGLA for 3D dose prediction. First, we propose a Gated Linear Attention-based UNet (GLAUNet) that incorporates an improved gating mechanism inspired by Mamba into linear attention to enhance global modeling capacity while retaining linear computational complexity. Second, a Wavelet-domain Constraint Loss (WDCL) is proposed to guide the model in learning inter-pixel relationship with better prediction contrasts in frequency domain. Experiments on the OpenKBP dataset show that our framework significantly outperforms the state-of-theart model with around 80% fewer parameters, achieving a Dose Score of 2.33 and a DVH Score of 1.46.

title: Optimize Flip Angle Schedules in Mr Fingerprinting using Reinforcement Learning
authors: Shenjun Zhong, Zhifeng Chen, Zhaolin Chen
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting (MRF) leverages transient-state signal dynamics generated by the tunable acquisition parameters, making the design of an optimal, robust sequence a complex, high-dimensional sequential decision problem, such as optimizing one of the key parameters, flip angle. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising approach to automate parameter selection, to optimize pulse sequences that maximize the distinguishability of fingerprints across the parameter space. In this work, we introduce an$R L$framework for optimizing the flip-angle schedule in MRF and demonstrate a learned schedule exhibiting non-periodic patterns that enhances fingerprint separability. Additionally, an interesting observation is that the$R L$-optimized schedule may enable a reduction in the number of repetition time, potentially accelerate MRF acquisitions.

title: Dual-Domain Hierarchical Adversarial Learning for Semi-Supervised Multi-View Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation and Disease Classification
authors: Kerong Zhou
abstract: Accurate prenatal screening for congenital heart disease (CHD) relies on fetal echocardiography, yet clinical interpretation is heavily operator-dependent and hampered by the scarcity of high-quality annotated multi-view data. To address these challenges, we propose a Dual-Domain Hierarchical Adversarial Learning (DD-HAL) framework for the 2026 ISBI Fetal HearT UltraSound Challenge. DD-HAL incorporates three core designs: a multi-view-shared and view-specific multi-branch encoder-decoder architecture, a hierarchical adversarial domain adaptation module, and a Mean-Teacher semi-supervised framework with consistency regularization, which simultaneously addresses multi-view heterogeneity, label scarcity, and domain shift. Our codes will be publicly available at https://github.com/SnapeLocke/DDHAL.

title: A Pipeline for DTI Indices and Connectivity Analysis Applied to a Longitudinal Multiple Sclerosis Cohort
authors: Liwei Zhou, Zhangxing Bian, Jinwei Zhang, Blake E. Dewey, Shiv Saidha, Peter A. Calabresi, Aaron Carass, Jerry L. Prince
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) causes progressive white matter damage, which can be sensitively assessed using diffusion MRI. However, existing analyses often rely on manual delineation, limiting scalability. We present an automated diffusion-MRI pipeline that computes global lesion-averaged DTI indices, tract-specific measures within tract-lesion intersections, and whole-brain structural connectivity metrics without manual intervention. The framework integrates lesion segmentation and filling, DWI preprocessing and DTI index computation, tractography reconstruction, bundle extraction, brain network analysis, and statistical analysis. Applied to a longitudinal MS cohort, the pipeline produced diffusion and connectivity patterns consistent with previously reported trends, supporting its validity. These results demonstrate the feasibility and practical utility of the proposed framework for scalable, longitudinal MS analysis.

title: Fedharmo: Harmonizing Global Aggregation and Local Alignment in Cross-Domain Federated Medical Image Segmentation
authors: You Zhou, Guangxia Cui, Shuchang Lyu, Guangliang Cheng, Lijiang Chen, Wenpei Bai, Qi Zhao 0037
abstract: Federated learning has emerged as the mainstream technique for breaking data silos in the healthcare domain by enabling collaborative training of machine learning models among different clients while ensuring data privacy. However, due to the discrepancy in the data distribution of each client, the aggregated model may ultimately be shifted towards certain clients. Consequently, we propose FedHarmo, a federated learning segmentation framework that employs an adaptive aggregation weight updating strategy to prevent model aggregation shifted towards certain clients. Additionally, we utilize the distribution measurement metric to minimize the distance between the global model and local models. Comprehensive experiments on ten medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Our code are available at https://github.com/GGbond-study/FedHarmo.

title: CBCT-Pose: Few-Shot Viewpoint-Conditioned Diffusion for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction
authors: Li Zhou 0014, Changsheng Fang, Bahareh Morovati, Shuo Han 0009, Shuyi Fan, Yu Shi, Hengyong Yu

title: Spinesynnet: Synthesis of Thin-Slice Spinal MR Images by a View-Prompt Elastic Deformation Network with Anatomical Constraint
authors: Jieying Zhou, Chaoqun Fu, Ting Sun, Yuhan Wang, Ao Jin, Zhihai Su, Hai Lu, Shumao Pang
abstract: Thin-slice spinal MR images are essential for precise segmentation but are clinically limited by long scan times and possible motion artifacts. Achieving the synthesis of thinslice spinal MR images from a given thick-slice MR scan is a promising solution to solve the aforementioned issues. However, due to the diversity of spinal structures and the lack of medical image data, this remains an unprecedented challenge. In this paper, we propose a novel approach named SpineSynNet for synthesizing thin-slice MR images from thick-slice scans by interpolating multiple intermediate slices of two adjacent thick slices. SpineSynNet is composed of a Viewprompt Deformation Field Estimation Module (VDFEM) and an anatomical constraint loss. The VDFEM is capable of expanding the training dataset by using multi-view inputs, and the anatomical constraint loss can ensure anatomical structural realism through the supervision of anatomical structure masks. During training, the SpineSynNet utilizes three views, including axial, coronal, and sagittal planes. Only the axial planes are employed in the inference stage. Experiments on 3D T2W-SPACE spinal MR volumetric images of 100 participants show that the proposed SpineSynNet achieves impressive performance with the PSNR and SSIM of$35.88 \pm 0.22$and$0.9458 \pm 0.0014$, respectively. The proposed method provides a promising tool for enhancing image inter-slice resolution, which has great potential in spinal structures segmentation in clinical applications.

title: DiSMemNet: Structure-Aware Distillation and Memory Network for Generalizable Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in EM Segmentation
authors: Ruining Zhou, Jinyue Guo, Liuyun Jiang, Jing Liu 0054, Hua Han 0001
abstract: Deep learning has greatly advanced electron microscopy (EM) segmentation, yet supervised models remain limited by costly voxel annotations and poor generalization across datasets with large domain shifts in contrast, texture, and morphology. These discrepancies distort both appearance and organelle topology, making structure-preserving adaptation essential for reliable EM analysis. To address this challenge, we propose DiSMemNet, a unified framework for unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) that jointly enhances appearance-structure alignment and cross-domain generalization.
